title: Trying On Silly Sunglasses In Tokyo
prompt:
Create a 30-second, ultra-realistic personal home video from the mid 2000s of two Japanese friends trying on ridiculous sunglasses at a street shop. Shot by one of them on a MiniDV camcorder.
FORMAT Six shots, 30s, five HARD CUTS, no fades. Every beat below is a separate shot and ends on a hard cut. The camera never dissolves or drifts between beats.
SUBJECTS AYA: Japanese woman, early twenties, shorter, round face, dark hair in a messy bun with strands escaping at the temples, oversized grey cardigan over a white tee, small stud earrings. She is the engine of the film — fast, physical, commits completely to every stupid idea, poses with total seriousness, talks with her hands, laughs with her whole upper body and has to hold onto something. RIN: Japanese woman, early twenties, taller, long straight black hair, dark green top, thin silver necklace. She is the opposite — economical, deadpan, moves once where Aya moves five times, reacts about a second later than everyone else, and her stillness while wearing something absurd is the funniest thing in the film. She never initiates, but she is the one who keeps handing Aya worse glasses. Faces, hair and clothing stay completely consistent throughout. Exactly these two appear, plus one shopkeeper.
LOCATION A small street stall in a Japanese shopping street, late afternoon. A rotating rack and a flat table covered in sunglasses — mirrored, oversized, heart-shaped, tiny ovals, novelty frames. A small propped mirror on the table. Awning overhead, shop fronts either side, the street behind with people passing.
CAMERA Mid-2000s MiniDV camcorder, handheld, held by whichever of them is not wearing the glasses. Natural shake, imperfect framing, autofocus hunting on shiny lenses, exposure blowing out toward the street, interlaced artefacts on fast movement, soft detail, mild noise, oversaturated colour, 4:3. The operator is an ordinary person, not a camera operator: they react late, cut off part of the subject, and the frame drops several inches whenever they laugh.
SHOT 1 — 0.0-5.0s. THE SPIN.
Both arrive at the stall from screen-left. AYA gets there first, plants both hands on the rotating rack and spins it hard — it clatters round twice and slows. She does not look at what she is taking; she reaches in blind, comes out with enormous white frames and puts them on in one movement, pushing them up her nose with one finger. Then she turns square to the lens, lifts her chin, and holds a completely serious model's expression, absolutely still, for two full seconds. RIN is off frame and starts laughing immediately; the camera drops four inches and comes back up. AYA does not break. HARD CUT.
SHOT 2 — 5.0-11.0s. THE ESCALATION.
RIN's hand comes in from screen-right holding out a worse pair — tiny oval lenses. AYA takes them without a word, swaps, and resumes exactly the same serious pose. The camera pushes in too close and the autofocus hunts twice on the lenses before settling. RIN's hand comes back a second time with heart-shaped frames. AYA, without breaking her expression, puts them on OVER the pair she is already wearing, so she is now wearing two. She turns her head slowly to the lens. The camera shakes hard with laughing and tilts. HARD CUT.
SHOT 3 — 11.0-16.0s. THE SWAP.
AYA's hand comes past the lens and takes the camera. The image swings wildly across the street and the shop front, blows out completely toward the sun, and settles unsteadily on RIN. RIN is already wearing huge mirrored aviators. She is standing perfectly still with both hands in her pockets, no expression at all, looking slightly off camera. After a beat she turns her head toward the lens — only her head, nothing else moves — and holds it. She does not smile. Her eyebrow goes up one millimetre. AYA is howling off frame and the camera is barely staying on her. HARD CUT.
SHOT 4 — 16.0-22.0s. THE MIRROR.
RIN picks up the small mirror off the table and turns it toward them both. They crowd in together, heads touching, shoulders squeezed, cheek to cheek, to look at once. Both see what they look like at the same moment. AYA breaks completely — she folds forward, grabs RIN's arm to stay upright, and her bun comes further undone. RIN holds for one more second, then takes her glasses off, looks at them, and puts them straight back on. The camera is being held out at arm's length by whoever has a spare hand — it is tilted, too close, and half of both faces are outside the frame. HARD CUT.
SHOT 5 — 22.0-27.0s. THE SHOPKEEPER.
An older woman in an apron walks in from screen-right without a word, reaches past both of them, picks one pair off the table and holds it out — the worst pair in the shop. Both of them stop dead. AYA takes them, puts them on, and turns to face her. The shopkeeper looks at her, nods once, satisfied, turns and walks back to her stool. She never smiles. AYA and RIN look at each other and both go. RIN actually laughs for the first time in the film. HARD CUT.
SHOT 6 — 27.0-30.0s. THE SELFIE.
They wedge together in front of the rack, still wearing everything, and hold the camcorder out at arm's length pointing back at themselves. The framing is bad — too close, tilted, RIN half out of frame on the right. AYA pulls a face and pushes her glasses down her nose to look over them. RIN looks straight into the lens with no expression whatsoever. Cuts abruptly to black mid-laugh. No fade.
PERFORMANCE Both are completely comfortable being filmed and forget it half the time. Every laugh is involuntary and physical, never posed for the camera. AYA's comedy comes from total commitment — she is never joking, she is modelling. RIN's comes from doing nothing at all. Neither of them mugs, gurns or performs to the lens. Everything spoken is in Japanese and not clearly audible over the ambience — no scripted lines, no subtitles, no on-screen text.
PHYSICAL REALISM Believable physics throughout. Hands, fingers, hair, fabric and eyewear behave naturally. No extra fingers, fused hands, duplicated limbs or distorted anatomy. No floating objects, teleportation, disappearing objects or sudden transformations. Sunglasses are separate physical objects with real weight — they sit on the nose and ears properly, slide down, get pushed up with a finger, and stay where they are put down. Worn pairs stay on the face until deliberately removed. The rack rotates with real momentum and rattles. The mirror reflects correctly. Hair moves and settles late. Feet stay properly connected to the ground.
AUDIO Natural environmental sound only. A rotating rack clattering, plastic frames on a table, both of them talking over each other in Japanese and laughing constantly, a street with people passing, a bicycle, distant shop music, camcorder handling noise and the operator's laughing distorting the mic. No music. No narration. No soundtrack.
POSITIVE LOCKS Six shots, five hard cuts, one cut at the end of every beat. AYA and RIN are the same two people in every shot, identical in face, hair and clothing. Exactly two friends and one shopkeeper appear. Glasses accumulate on AYA and are never silently removed between shots. Every shot ends on a hard cut and the next begins on a new framing.
FINAL FEEL A real tape somebody's friend shot and forgot about. Bright, loud and very funny. The joy comes from how much they are enjoying each other — the spinning rack, the escalating glasses, Rin's dead-straight face, the mirror, the shopkeeper joining in and winning. Prioritise natural behaviour, consistent identity, believable physics and imperfect handheld framing.

title: City Beat Driven Cinematic Reel
prompt:
Simply replace [CITY]:
"Create a 15-second, 4K, 16:9 ultra-fast cinematic city reel of [CITY]. Every second counts. High energy, beat-driven, visually addictive. Every shot has camera movement. Nothing is ever static.
OPENING TITLE (0–2.5s)
A stunning wide cinematic clip of [CITY] plays in the background — drone over the skyline, golden streets, or iconic landmark — camera slowly pushing in. Over this, the city name [CITY] appears large, filling 70–80% of the screen. Font culturally matched to the city. Color tied to the city's identity — Barcelona: deep yellow/gold, Tokyo: red, Paris: soft blue, New York: orange. Text holds 1.5 seconds then dissolves. The background clip keeps playing seamlessly into the next act.
ACT 1 — BUILD (2.5–7s)
4–5 fast clips, each 0.8–1 second. Pace is aggressive from the start. Mix of:
•Drone banking hard over rooftops
•Slow-mo street crowd, markets, people in motion
•Fast tracking shot through a busy alley or square
•One detail shot — food, texture, architecture, color
Every cut lands on the beat. Camera always moving — whip pans, snap tilts, fast push-ins.
ACT 2 — PEAK (7–12s)
The drop. Maximum energy. Use at least one:
•Rapid flash cuts: 6–8 clips in 2 seconds, each on the beat — landmarks, faces, food, streets, pure color — sensory overload
•Screen split stack: 3 clips tiling the screen simultaneously showing different sides of [CITY], then collapsing into one
•Beat stacks: clips slamming on top of each other one by one with each musical hit, then wiping clean
This is the heart of the reel. Maximum visual density. Every frame a different texture, color, energy.
FINAL HOLD (12–15s)
One last punch of 2–3 fast clips, then — the most stunning shot [CITY] has. Aerial skyline, iconic waterfront, magic hour view. Camera slowly rising. Music resolves. Fade to black.
TECHNICAL: 4K, 16:9, 24fps with 120fps slow-mo on select shots. Anamorphic lens feel, subtle flares, slight vignette. Zero static shots.
COLOR: Match to [CITY]'s soul — warm teal-orange for Mediterranean, cool blue for northern European, vivid saturated for tropical and Latin cities, neon high-contrast for nightlife capitals.
MUSIC: Fast catchy beat, culturally influenced by [CITY]'s country. Every cut locked to the music.
NO voiceover. NO text after the opening title. NO static shots.
Feel: 15 seconds that make your heart race. You lived in [CITY]. You need to go.

title: Fashion Ten Pose Editorial Film
prompt:
Create a 15-second high-fashion editorial film starring the adult character in @[char ref]. Preserve their exact appearance, outfit, accessories and visual style. Render the entire film in the reference's aesthetic.
Use a minimal studio with a reflective floor, bold directional lighting and rhythmic photographic flashes.
Show exactly 10 distinct fashion poses, each with a different silhouette and camera angle:
1. A confident standing pose, filmed from floor level with dramatic wide-angle perspective.
2. One hand beside the face, captured in an extreme side-profile close-up.
3. An asymmetric seated pose, seen directly overhead as the camera rotates.
4. One leg extended toward the lens, the foot or reference footwear dominating the foreground through foreshortening.
5. A quick, fluid leg cross, captured from a low diagonal angle.
6. Fingertips catching the edge of an existing sleeve or collar, framed in a tight detail shot.
7. A rear three-quarter turn with a deliberate glance back into the camera.
8. A forward lean toward the lens, ending with the palm briefly covering it.
9. An elongated upward stretch, revealed in a sharply tilted wide shot with strong side lighting.
10. A commanding full-body hero pose, looking down into the lens as the camera rapidly pulls back.
Keep the performance fast and rhythmically tight. Flow naturally between poses, holding each for only a fraction of a second while keeping its silhouette clearly readable. No repeated poses or additional pose changes.
Connect angles through whip pans, movement-matched cuts, snap zooms, flashes and lens occlusions. Orbit against the character's turn, sweep from their floor reflection toward their face and plunge from overhead to floor level. Alternate intimate details with dramatic wide compositions. Cinematic live-action emotional reaction scene, vertical 9:16 format, approximately 20 seconds, intimate static tripod camera with hard editorial cuts between close-ups. She looks down at the box, then slowly lifts her eyes toward the unseen person off-screen. Her eyebrows rise and her lips part with genuine surprise. She says softly, with confused delight: “This is for me? Why?” The camera remains still. Warm window light falls across her face and pink silk camisole.

She holds the box steady on her lap and whispers with a fragile laugh: “Wait — if I cry, this is your fault.” Her voice is soft, slightly thick, and emotionally restrained.

She takes one careful breath, holds it briefly, and opens the lid completely. Include the soft rustle of wrapping paper and a delicate metallic clink from inside the box. Her eyes remain slightly pink along the lower lash line.
CUT.

Extreme close-up from mid-forehead to just below the chin. Clara looks down into the open box, contents mostly out of frame. Her pupils move as she reads or recognizes what is inside. Extreme close-up of only her eyes and the bridge of her nose. Her eyes drop toward the open box below frame. Her eyelids lower and lashes fan down. Then her eyes snap back up, widening with recognition rather than shock. Her iris catches the warm window light. The pink rim remains delicate and contained. She whispers, barely audible: “Oh no — no, you didn’t.”

Tight-to-medium close-up, forehead to chest. Clara pulls the open gift box close against the pink silk of her camisole and wraps both arms around it. Her eyes glisten. She lets out a shaky breath, then a real affectionate smile breaks across her face, showing her teeth. Her lower eyelids lift and crinkle naturally. title: Not A Great Start To The Morning
prompt:
30-second continuous photorealistic candid home-video scene in a quiet Korean residential neighborhood on a warm summer morning. The entire video must look like genuine footage recorded by a friend in the early 2000s, NOT a commercial, movie, music video or AI-generated scene.
CHARACTER CONSISTENCY:
Use the supplied character reference sheet as the strict visual reference for all characters.
MAIN GIRL: Minji, 21, young Korean woman, natural realistic face, authentic skin texture, messy wavy black hair loosely tied back. Oversized plain white T-shirt, loose light pajama pants and simple flat sandals. Keep exactly the same face, hairstyle, clothing, age and body proportions throughout.
FRIEND: Jisung, 22, remains behind the camera for the entire video. Only his natural male voice and laughter are heard.
NEIGHBOR: Mrs. Park, elderly Korean woman around 70, same appearance as reference, wearing comfortable patterned house clothes.
Two school children appear briefly in the background wearing ordinary school clothes and backpacks.
LOCATION:
A real lived-in older Korean residential lane: narrow concrete road, modest houses, aged walls, potted plants, bicycles, laundry, utility poles and overhead wires. Warm natural morning sunlight. Nothing staged or overly picturesque.
CAMERA:
Entire video is filmed by Jisung using an old handheld early-2000s consumer DV camcorder. Genuine handheld shake, slightly imperfect framing, small accidental pans, occasional autofocus adjustment, mild exposure breathing, faded DV colors, soft digital detail, subtle compression noise and realistic motion blur.
The camera operator reacts physically to events. Do NOT use cinematic camera movement, gimbal stabilization, slow motion, drone shots, perfect composition, dramatic depth of field or modern commercial color grading.
SEQUENCE — ONE NATURAL CONTINUOUS EVENT:
[0–4 SEC]
Minji casually walks out of her house holding a green garden hose and begins watering several potted plants beside the entrance.
She notices Jisung filming her and looks directly toward the camera with a small amused smile.
MINJI, natural Korean-accented English:
“Why are you filming this?”
JISUNG, casually from behind camera:
“I’m bored.”
She gives him a playful annoyed look, then continues watering.
[4–9 SEC]
The water pressure gradually becomes weak and then almost stops.
Minji looks at the hose nozzle, confused. She lightly shakes it once and squeezes the nozzle again.
Nothing.
She follows the hose with her eyes and notices that part of the hose is accidentally trapped underneath her own sandal.
Her reaction is subtle and completely natural.
[9–13 SEC]
Minji casually lifts her foot off the hose.
IMMEDIATELY the normal water pressure returns.
A sudden stream of water shoots upward from the badly angled nozzle and splashes directly across her face, hair and upper T-shirt.
IMPORTANT: realistic garden-hose physics only. No explosive or exaggerated water.
Minji freezes for a moment in genuine surprise.
Jisung instinctively jerks the camera sideways, briefly losing the framing, then quickly points it back toward her while laughing.
Minji slowly looks directly at the camera with an embarrassed “seriously?” expression.
[13–18 SEC]
Laughing, Minji turns the hose toward Jisung as if she is going to spray him.
While adjusting the nozzle she accidentally rotates it the wrong direction.
A short stronger spray hits her own shoulder and face AGAIN.
She immediately recoils and laughs:
“Wait—wait!”
Jisung laughs harder behind the camera. His laughter makes the handheld framing noticeably shakier.
Minji is genuinely laughing now, slightly soaked, with wet strands of hair naturally sticking around her face.
[18–23 SEC]
Mrs. Park, the elderly neighbor who has been tending plants near her doorway, notices what happened.
Minji looks toward her, embarrassed but laughing.
Mrs. Park smiles and raises her own small garden hose as though she is going to help.
Minji relaxes.
Instead, Mrs. Park gives Minji ONE quick, harmless playful spray of water.
Minji looks completely shocked for half a second.
Then Mrs. Park laughs.
Minji immediately starts laughing too.
[23–27 SEC]
Minji playfully sprays a small amount of water back toward Mrs. Park.
Mrs. Park laughs and steps behind her gate.
Two school children walking farther down the lane notice the situation, stop briefly and laugh naturally before continuing.
Keep this spontaneous and subtle — NOT a large staged water fight.
[27–30 SEC]
Still laughing and visibly wet, Minji walks directly toward Jisung and the camera while holding the hose.
She points at him and says:
“You started this.”
JISUNG replies while laughing:
“I literally did nothing!”
Minji gives him a mischievous look and sends ONE quick spray directly toward the camera.
Water hits the camcorder lens.
The image instantly becomes partially blurred and smeared by realistic water droplets while the camera operator reacts.
Minji’s genuine laughter remains audible through the wet blurry image.
HARD CUT.
REALISM / PERFORMANCE:
All people must look and move like real humans captured unexpectedly on a home video. Natural blinking, breathing, posture, weight shifts, imperfect timing, realistic hand movements and restrained facial expressions.
Dialogue must sound like REAL HUMAN SPEECH: natural young adult voices, normal conversational volume, correct emotional timing, subtle Korean accents, no robotic cadence, no narrator voice, no exaggerated acting. Characters must speak ONLY their assigned dialogue. No extra dialogue.
The humor comes entirely from the believable accident and genuine reactions. Nobody behaves like an actor performing a comedy sketch.
WATER PHYSICS:
Water must behave exactly like real garden-hose water: correct gravity, splash direction, droplets, wet fabric and progressively wetter hair. The hose stays physically connected and maintains consistent shape. No disappearing hose, duplicated hose, impossible water sources or changing nozzle.
CONTINUITY:
Minji becomes progressively wetter after each splash and must remain wet afterward. Her clothing, face, hairstyle, house, hose and neighborhood remain consistent. Mrs. Park remains the same person. School children remain consistent. No character duplication, sudden wardrobe changes, teleportation, object morphing or discontinuous positions.
AUDIO:
Absolutely NO music and NO narration.
Only authentic location sound: birds, distant neighborhood conversations, faint traffic, footsteps on concrete, occasional bicycle sound, running water, hose splashes, clothing movement and genuine laughter.
FINAL LOOK:
Warm summer morning, nostalgic early-2000s Korean home-video feeling. Slightly faded DV colors, ordinary natural sunlight and imperfect consumer-camera quality.
The finished video should feel like a funny forgotten family camcorder recording from a real summer morning — completely spontaneous, mundane, charming and physically believable.

title: POV: 15 Seconds of a 2000s Korean Summer
prompt:
Duration: 15s | Aspect Ratio: 16:9
Style: Ultra-realistic early-2000s Korean MiniDV home video, nostalgic documentary realism, natural handheld camera, faded colors, soft DV sharpness, autofocus hunting, exposure pumping, motion blur, digital compression, no stabilization, no modern cinematic grading.
MAIN CHARACTER: Young Korean man, early 20s, slim-average build, short slightly messy black hair, clean-shaven, natural skin texture. Faded white oversized T-shirt, loose blue jeans, worn white canvas sneakers, black wristwatch. Keep identical face, hairstyle, outfit and proportions throughout.
SETTING: Authentic early-2000s Korean neighborhood—narrow concrete alleys, low-rise houses, bicycles, utility poles, small shops, school playground, riverside and rooftop. No smartphones, modern cars, LED screens or modern advertising.
0–1.5s
Bright summer morning. He wakes up, opens bedroom window and sunlight floods in. Cicadas and birds outside. Quick handheld cut.
1.5–3s
He rides an old bicycle through a quiet Korean alley. Camera follows shakily from behind. He turns and briefly smiles.
3–4.5s
Tiny neighborhood convenience store. He grabs a cold bottled drink, takes a sip outside. His friend steals a sip and he laughs.
4.5–6s
Outdoor basketball court. He shoots—SWISH. He celebrates toward the camera as his friend laughs.
6–7.5s
Riverside. He rides beside the water, stops, throws a small stone. SPLASH.
7.5–9s
Sitting outside a small shop eating ice cream. Ice cream accidentally gets on his lip. Friend points the camera at him; he notices and laughs.
9–10.5s
Sudden summer water fight. Friends spray him with a garden hose. He grabs it and sprays them back. Chaotic handheld laughter.
10.5–12s
Warm sunset. He walks home beside his bicycle through the same neighborhood, quieter now. Cicadas continue.
12–13.5s
Night rooftop. He and friends watch distant fireworks. Firework light briefly illuminates their faces. One friend says naturally: “여름 진짜 좋다.” (“Summer is really nice.”)
13.5–15s
Final handheld shot: he runs down the neighborhood street at night, turns toward camera laughing. Motion blur → brief MiniDV glitch → abrupt black.
AUDIO: Only natural sounds—cicadas, birds, bicycle chain, footsteps, basketball, shop ambience, water splashing, laughter and fireworks. No background music.
REALISM: Every cut must feel like a genuine memory recorded by a friend. Same character throughout, realistic physics, spontaneous expressions, hard cuts only, no flashy transitions, no text, no subtitles, no watermark, no modern cinematic effects.

title: Vampire AI Girlfriend Midnight Mood
prompt:
一、人物
核心人物：阿黎（女主）
年轻女性，约21岁，鹅蛋脸，皮肤白皙通透，长棕黑色微卷长发及胸，发丝蓬松有层次感。正常状态：棕色瞳孔，眼神温柔，嘴唇饱满涂淡粉色口红，面带甜美微笑，气质清纯治愈。觉醒状态：双眼变为鲜红色发光瞳孔（全红眼，虹膜发出红色微光），嘴角微张露出一对尖锐小虎牙/尖牙（吸血鬼特征），眉头微皱，表情从温柔转为诡异、慑人。身穿浅灰色宽松连帽卫衣（oversize，面料柔软有棉绒质感），下搭黑色运动短裤（裤脚边缘白色镶边），赤脚。身形纤细，锁骨明显。
POV角色（男友/观众视角）
仅露出手和前臂，皮肤偏白，穿深色衣物，在视频后半段从背后伸出右手抓住阿黎的左臂。不露面，全程第一人称主观视角。
二、物品
大床：深灰色/炭灰色被子和床单，凌乱褶皱（有人刚离开的痕迹）
金属落地衣架：黑色铁艺，挂着黑色外套、灰色大衣等几件衣物
床头柜：左侧矮柜，上面放暖黄色小台灯（点亮状态，暖光光源）
落地玻璃推拉门：大面积黑色细框玻璃门，通向阳台
阳台：黑色金属栏杆（竖条式），水泥/瓷砖地面
白色纱帘：窗户两侧半透明白色纱帘，轻微飘动
窗外：城市夜景，密集建筑万家灯火（暖黄/白色光点），夜空中一轮明亮圆月
阿黎赤脚，无鞋
三、场景与环境
场景一：高层公寓卧室（前半段，约0-30秒）
现代简约风格高层公寓卧室，空间紧凑温馨。左侧是金属衣架和床头柜（暖黄台灯），中间是大床（深灰床品），右侧/后方是大面积落地玻璃推拉门，可看到窗外城市夜景和月亮。室内光线偏暗，主要靠台灯暖光照明，窗外月光和城市灯光透过玻璃渗入。
场景二：公寓阳台（后半段，约36-59秒）
卧室外的小阳台，黑色金属栏杆，水泥地面，空间狭窄。前方是无遮挡的城市夜景视野，密集的高楼灯火延伸至远方，夜空深蓝，一轮圆月高悬。夜风吹动，氛围清冷孤寂。
四、精准动作说明与动态表现
时间线（约59秒）：
时间 动作
0-5秒 阿黎趴在床上，上半身撑起，面向镜头（POV），甜美微笑，右手抬起伸向镜头，手掌遮住镜头（调皮互动），手指自然张开
5-10秒 阿黎放下手，左手抚摸自己的脸颊，开心大笑，露出牙齿，眼睛弯成月牙，身体微微晃动

动态细节：

红眼觉醒时眼睛有轻微红色光晕脉动

女人极近景，脸占据画面大部分，不能变形。背景只剩模糊的雨声、木门暗影和一盏颤动的残灯。她的眼睛微微睁大，像是第一次听见真相，却不愿立刻相信。

原生生成中文对白，严格区分两位说话者，口型与每个音节准确同步。男人声音低沉沙哑、克制疲惫；女人声音清冷锐利，后段出现轻微颤音。保留真实换气、吞咽、衣料湿重摩擦、剑柄轻响、破庙木梁风声、远处雨声和烛火细微燃烧声。不要背景音乐，不要旁白，不要字幕，不要夸张武打音效。
【影像限制】
不要全身镜头，不要远景，不要大规模打斗，不要飞天动作。不要字幕、不要任何可读文字、不要水印、不要 Logo。不要新增第三个人物，不要切换场景，不要改变服装和发型，不要面孔漂移，不要美颜磨皮，不要现代物品，不要夸张肢体动作，不要慢动作，不要快速环绕镜头，不要商业广告灯光，不要异常牙齿、嘴唇粘连、口型错位、目光漂移或不自然流泪。

title: Coolant Tech Galactic City Day

An intimate slice-of-life montage follows Tavi Rell, an ordinary municipal coolant technician, through one working day in a crowded, weathered galactic city. Tavi has cropped dark hair, a faded rust-colored work jacket, charcoal clothes, and a worn tool satchel. Keep this identity and outfit consistent.
Use objective third-person observational cinematography with an unstabilized shoulder-mounted camera and natural 28-40mm lens perspective. The camera has no in-world owner and never represents another person’s viewpoint. No POV, first-person perspective, over-the-shoulder framing, body camera, vlog, found footage, surveillance imagery, or interaction with the lens. Characters never notice or acknowledge the camera.
The handheld quality comes only from restrained micro-jitter, low-frequency shoulder drift, slight horizon wander, small reframing delays, soft focus breathing, and brief reactive pans. Compositions remain intentional and readable. Avoid aggressive shaking, floating motion, perfect stabilization, smooth gimbal tracking, cranes, and drones.
0-3 seconds: Medium-wide front three-quarter view from the apartment corner. A low cargo vessel shakes the room; the frame trembles with the vibration and makes a quick imperfect tilt toward a falling metal cup as Tavi catches it near the floor.
3-4 seconds: Hard cut on the catch to a ground-level profile insert. Tavi tightens a worn boot while a palm-sized cleaning robot crosses the foreground, briefly pulling focus away.
4-6 seconds: Wide lateral view inside a crowded residential lift. The loosely held frame drifts between Tavi, a sleepy amphibious neighbor, and an overloaded utility robot as the lift rattles downward.
6-8 seconds: The opening lift doors create a hard location cut to a steaming street market. Rear three-quarter medium tracking keeps Tavi visible through passing bodies; the framing lags slightly when Tavi turns toward a food vendor.
8-10 seconds: Side-profile medium shot inside a vibrating commuter hover-bus. Vehicle movement creates natural handheld vibration while Tavi watches towers, dense traffic, and an immense carrier pass beyond the window.
10-11 seconds: Frontal medium two-shot at a routine checkpoint. A helmeted officer scans Tavi’s work pass; the camera makes a small late pan from the scanner light to Tavi’s tired reaction.
11-14 seconds: Side medium-close view in a narrow service tunnel. The camera loosely tracks between Tavi’s face and hands as a leaking coolant pipe is welded shut; bright sparks cause brief focus breathing and exposure fluctuation.
14-16 seconds: Hard cut through the sparks to a wide rooftop lunch view. Wind creates subtle shoulder drift; when two interceptor craft roar overhead, the camera makes a quick imperfect pan upward, then settles back on Tavi continuing to eat.
16-17 seconds: Profile close-up. Focus shifts from a small blue family hologram floating above Tavi’s palm to the quiet smile forming on Tavi’s face.
17-19 seconds: Lateral medium tracking through a dense evening parts bazaar. Foreground shoppers and hanging cables briefly obscure the frame as Tavi tests and purchases a secondhand power coupling.
19-21 seconds: Low front three-quarter two-shot in an apartment corridor. Tavi installs the coupling into an elderly neighbor’s damaged service robot; the handheld frame follows the rotating head, then returns to Tavi’s relieved expression.
21-23 seconds: Graphic match to laundry rotating inside a scratched communal cleaning drum. A nearly static medium shot retains gentle shoulder drift as Tavi waits among chatting residents, half asleep with the tool satchel between both feet.
23-24 seconds: Hard cut to a profile medium-close shot beside a battered tavern game machine. Colored bulbs flash, and a brief reactive reframing catches Tavi’s surprised expression without becoming subjective.
24-26 seconds: Loose medium group shot at the crowded bar. Tavi shares a cheap drink and quiet laughter with two exhausted coworkers while passing patrons naturally cross and partially obscure the foreground.
26-30 seconds: Wide side-profile view on the apartment roof at night. Tavi waters one stubborn plant beneath two moons and busy orbital traffic. The handheld frame breathes gently in the wind but remains detached and observational. A kettle whistles inside; Tavi picks up the satchel and exits. The camera holds on the plant and distant ships with a faint imperfect drift.
Use only clean diegetic location sound: engines, room vibration, market chatter, scanner chirps, robotic beeps, welding crackle, traffic, tavern murmur, rooftop wind, and the final kettle whistle. No camera handling noise, operator footsteps, breathing near the microphone, dialogue, BGM, or subtitles. Keep recognizable franchise names, logos, characters, and designs absent.

title: City Cat Cafe Morning Commute
prompt:
风格：*现代都市真人写实、自然晨光、轻纪录片质感  
镜头结构：第三人称；人物整体从画面左侧向右侧移动
## 人物与场景
28 岁左右的都市女性，黑色低马尾，淡妆，真实自然肤质。穿米白色短款风衣、浅蓝衬衫、深灰直筒西裤和低跟皮鞋。
棕色斜挎通勤包的肩带从右肩斜跨至左腰，包体固定在左侧腰后方，蹲下和起身时不滑落。左手始终拿着纸杯咖啡，右腕佩戴简洁手表，右手负责与小猫互动。
工作日上午八点左右，现代公寓外的人行道。远处有早餐店、共享单车、通勤人群和缓慢驶过的车辆。昨夜下过小雨，路面略带湿润反光。清晨阳光从建筑间斜射下来，光线柔和自然。
树池边坐着一只体型偏小的橘白猫，右耳有一个小缺口，毛发稍显蓬松。小猫保持真实动物习性，最初警惕，确认安全后才主动靠近。
## 0.0–2.6 秒｜快步出门
**镜头一：35mm 中景，稳定器侧向跟拍。**
公寓玻璃门向外打开，女主从门内快步走出，沿人行道从画面左侧向右侧行走。她身体略微前倾，步速偏快，呈现普通上班族赶时间的状态。
走出两步后，她低头看一眼右腕手表。右手只轻微抬起，不停下来，也不夸张皱眉。她确认时间后嘴唇轻抿，继续向前走。
左手咖啡杯保持稳定，斜挎包固定在左腰后方，不换手、不晃动。
**声音：**玻璃门回弹声、连续脚步声、远处车辆声和早餐店模糊交谈声。
## 2.6–4.6 秒｜听见猫叫，停下脚步
镜头继续侧向跟拍。
树池方向传来一声轻短的“喵”。
女主正准备迈出的右脚自然减速，最终轻轻落地。她的视线先移向画面右下方，停顿一瞬，头部才跟着转过去。
她看见小猫后，原本紧绷的肩膀随着一次轻微呼气稍稍放松。嘴唇不再抿紧，但暂时不露出明显笑容。
镜头停止跟拍，轻微向右摇动，将女主和树池旁的小猫同时纳入画面，交代两者距离。
**表演重点：**声音先出现，随后才有减速、视线移动和转头反应；人物不能在猫叫前提前看向小猫。
## 4.6–8.5 秒｜蹲下，等待小猫靠近
**镜头二：50mm 低机位中近景，女主位于左侧，小猫位于右侧。**
女主向树池靠近半步，保持咖啡杯在左手，屈膝缓慢蹲下。她的身体停在距离小猫约半米的位置，不继续逼近。
她缓慢伸出右手，手背朝上，停在小猫鼻尖前约十厘米的位置。手伸到位后保持不动，不主动触碰小猫。

title: Aesthetic Cafe Vlog Disaster
prompt:
Create a 30-second, 1080p ultra-realistic personal home-video showing a young Korean woman attempting to film an "aesthetic" café vlog for her social media and everything comically not going to plan. No reference image.
MAIN SUBJECT
Young Korean woman in her early 20s, trendy and put-together look, dewy makeup, confident expression that keeps cracking into laughter.
Straight black hair with curtain bangs, small gold hoop earrings, soft pink lip tint.
Wearing an oversized cream sweater, a plaid mini skirt, chunky white sneakers, and a small quilted shoulder bag she keeps adjusting for the "shot."
Maintain the same face, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions, and appearance throughout the entire video.
SETTING
A charming autumn café street in Seoul on a crisp, sunny afternoon.
A cozy corner café with outdoor seating, string lights, a chalkboard menu, falling ginkgo leaves, a latte art station visible through the window, a bicycle propped against a brick wall, pedestrians occasionally walking through frame, and a small tree dropping leaves onto the sidewalk table. Warm, golden, Pinterest-looking — until it isn't.
CAMERA / VISUAL AESTHETIC
Raw personal footage, filmed by her friend who keeps trying (and failing) to make it look cinematic, strong handheld vlog shake throughout.
The video oscillates between deliberately "aesthetic" attempted shots — slow pans, artful angles, soft focus — and sudden chaotic handheld jolts when things go wrong. Autofocus hunts comically between her face and the latte. Camera tilts and overcorrects. Exposure blows out when it swings toward the sun. Mild motion blur during quick recoveries. Slightly warm, oversaturated color grade like a try-hard Instagram filter that keeps slipping back to raw reality.
No stabilization, no real cinematic polish — the "aesthetic" is aspirational, the execution is not.
00:00–00:05 — THE PERFECT LATTE SHOT (ATTEMPT)
She sits at the outdoor table, carefully positioning a latte with foam art, trying to casually "candid" sip it for the camera.
The camera does a slow artful pan down toward the cup — then a leaf falls directly into it with a soft plop.
She freezes, staring at the ruined latte art, deadpan.
00:05–00:10 — REACTION
She looks up at the camera, unimpressed, leaf still floating in the foam.
"...Are you kidding me right now."
The friend behind the camera bursts out laughing, shaking the frame violently.
00:10–00:15 — THE "CANDID" WALK
She gets up to attempt a slow-motion aesthetic walk past the café window, hair flowing, sunglasses going on in one smooth motion — sunglasses immediately get caught in her hair.
She stops mid-stride, wincing, trying to untangle them one-handed while still smiling for the camera.
The camera zooms in awkwardly close on the tangled sunglasses, then yanks back out.
00:15–00:20 — BICYCLE MISHAP
She leans against the parked bicycle for a "casual candid lean" pose, one hand in her pocket.
The bicycle kickstand gives way and it slowly tips sideways, taking her balance with it.
She stumbles but catches herself, laughing hard, one hand up defensively toward the lens.
"Okay, delete that, delete that!"
00:20–00:25 — GINKGO LEAF CHAOS
She tries to recreate a "leaves falling around me" cinematic moment by tossing a handful of gathered ginkgo leaves into the air above her head.
A gust of wind blows them straight back into her face instead.
She spits out a leaf, blinking, completely unbothered and giggling.
The camera shakes as the operator nearly drops it laughing.
00:25–00:30 — FINAL MOMENT
She gives up on the aesthetic altogether, plops back down at the café table, and grabs the leaf-ruined latte anyway, taking a defiant sip through the foam.
She looks dead into the camera, deadpan, leaf still stuck to her sweater.
"This is the content. This is it. Post this one."
She gives an exaggerated thumbs up as the frame shakes with the friend's laughter, and the footage cuts abruptly to black.
AUDIO
Natural location sound only:
Café ambience, cup clinking, leaves rustling, wind gusts, bicycle clattering, footsteps, her friend's audible laughter throughout, fabric rustling, and handheld camera noise.
No music. No narration. No artificial sound effects.
Spoken lines: "...Are you kidding me right now." / "Okay, delete that, delete that!" / "This is the content. This is it. Post this one."
FINAL FEEL
A self-aware, comedic behind-the-scenes of someone trying to film an aesthetic vlog and getting completely humbled by reality at every turn — warm, golden autumn light paired with genuine, unscripted chaos and laughter.
No posed perfection sustained for more than a few seconds before something goes wrong. No exaggerated slapstick acting — the comedy comes from real reactions, real mishaps, and the gap between the "vision" and what actually happens on camera.

title: That Summer Day — Korean Neighborhood DV Camcorder
prompt:
MAIN SUBJECT
Young Korean woman in her early 20s, naturally attractive, realistic skin texture, minimal makeup, relaxed and approachable personality. Long dark hair loosely tied into a messy side ponytail, natural facial expressions. Wearing a fitted pastel blue fitted short top, loose cream pajama-style pants, black sneakers and a simple silver necklace. Maintain the same face, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions and overall appearance throughout.
LOCATION
A quiet older Korean residential neighborhood during a warm summer afternoon. Narrow concrete lanes, low-rise homes, small gardens, bicycles, potted plants, utility poles, overhead wires, old staircases, a small neighborhood bakery and a public water tap. No tourist attractions, advertisements, recognizable brands, crowds or commercial activity.
CAMERA / VISUAL STYLE
Raw personal footage casually recorded by a friend on an early-2000s consumer DV camcorder. Natural handheld shake, imperfect framing, autofocus hunting, exposure shifts, slight motion blur, faded colors, soft image detail, mild digital noise and occasional accidental zooms. No stabilization, gimbal movement, drone shots or polished commercial cinematography.
— OUTSIDE HOME
She sits on the concrete stairs outside her home, slowly eating a bright orange cola-flavored ice pop. She looks down the quiet lane, takes another bite and smiles toward the camera.
— SMALL ERRAND
She gets up, stretches casually and walks toward a nearby neighborhood bakery carrying a small reusable bag. She passes a bicycle and gives a small wave to an elderly neighbor sitting outside.
— BAKERY STOP
She buys a warm pastry, steps outside and takes a small bite immediately. She smiles at the camera, wipes a few crumbs from her fingers and starts walking home.
— LITTLE INTERRUPTION
A small neighborhood cat suddenly crosses her path and stops beside a garden wall. She pauses, crouches down and gently pets it. The cat brushes against her leg before walking away.
— QUIET WALK
She continues down the lane beneath large leafy trees. A soft breeze moves her hair and clothes. She walks slowly, eating the pastry while watching the quiet street around her.
— FINAL MOMENT
She reaches the stairs outside her home, turns toward the camera with a relaxed smile and says:
"That was a good afternoon."
She sits back down on the stairs, takes one final bite and gives a small wave.
The camera remains on her for a moment before the recording naturally cuts to black.
AUDIO: Natural environmental audio only — birds, insects, footsteps, bicycle bells, distant scooters, wind through trees, quiet conversations, bakery sounds, cat sounds and subtle camcorder-handling noise. No music, narration or soundtrack.
FINAL FEEL: A forgotten recording of an ordinary Korean summer afternoon — slow, warm, intimate, nostalgic, slightly imperfect and spontaneous. The beauty comes from everyday routines, natural expressions, quiet streets and small interactions. No posing, exaggerated reactions or polished cinematic shots.

prompt:
ULTRA REALISTIC 30 SECOND PERSONAL HOME VIDEO. 1080p render of 4:3 early 2000s MiniDV tape footage. Single continuous handheld take, no cuts. Title: THE 9PM RAMYEON RUN.
CONCEPT: A young Korean woman makes a late evening convenience store run. Nothing happens. Her friend holds the camcorder and films her the way friends actually film each other, badly and without a plan. She talks to the friend, never to a lens, never to an audience.
SUBJECT LOCK: Korean woman, early twenties. Realistic skin with visible pores, faint under eye shadow, minimal makeup, slight shine on the forehead under store lighting. Dark brown hair loosely tied back with strands falling loose at the temples. Oversized cream knit sweater with stretched cuffs, blue jeans, white sneakers scuffed at the toe, small canvas shoulder bag worn across the body. Same face, same hair, same outfit held identically for the full 30 seconds. Relaxed genuine personality, unposed posture, weight shifting on one hip when standing still.
SETTING: Small 24 hour convenience store on a quiet older Seoul residential street, cool autumn night. Fluorescent ceiling tubes, one flickering slightly. Crowded shelves, handwritten price tags, a hot water dispenser, a narrow window counter facing the street. Outside the glass, wet dark asphalt, parked scooters, a shuttered shop, occasional headlights sweeping past. Lived in and unstyled. No visible brands, no logos, no readable signage anywhere in frame.
CAMERA: Raw handheld MiniDV camcorder held by a friend walking alongside her. Constant autofocus hunting, especially on steam and on the glass. Exposure pumping as she moves between the store lighting and the dark window. Awkward unmotivated zoom in and back out. Subject drifts off center and out of frame for a beat before the operator corrects. Mild tape noise, interlace combing on fast movement, one brief tape dropout glitch. Handheld micro shake, no stabilization, no gimbal, no cinematic choreography, no rack focus, no dolly language.
BEATS: 0:00 to 0:05 Exterior. Camera follows her from behind as she pushes the glass door open, door chime, operator fumbles a zoom on the way in.
0:05 to 0:12 Aisle. She picks up two cups of instant noodles, compares them, puts one back. Camera loses her behind a shelf for two seconds, then finds her again.
0:12 to 0:19 Hot water dispenser. Steam rises, autofocus hunts badly on the steam. She waits, taps the lid twice, glances at the camera and looks away.
0:19 to 0:25 Window counter. She eats standing, mouth full, offers the cup toward the lens and speaks the first line, then laughs at herself and pulls it back.
0:25 to 0:30 Dead air. She chews and watches the street through the glass. Nobody speaks for three full seconds. Then she says the second line, laughs, and the camera swings down toward the floor as the tape cuts.
DIALOGUE: Spoken language locked to Korean. Only two lines in the entire clip.

title: Shanghai Jewelry Cinematic Drama

title: Ordinary Day Cinematic Vlog
prompt:
Create a 30-second, 1080p ultra-realistic personal home-video of a young Korean woman confidently claiming she can sing, only to completely fall apart mid-song in a noraebang (karaoke room). No reference image.
MAIN SUBJECT
Young Korean woman in her early 20s, casual and confident energy, natural makeup that's slightly smudged from a night out, expressive face that goes from cocky to distressed in seconds.
Long black hair in loose waves, a claw clip half-holding it up, small hoop earrings catching the disco light.
Wearing an oversized denim jacket over a graphic tee, black mini skirt, ankle boots, holding a wireless karaoke mic like it's a real microphone.
Maintain the same face, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions, and appearance throughout the entire video.
SETTING
A small, slightly worn private noraebang room late at night.
Neon-colored wall lighting cycling through pink, blue, and purple, a low vinyl couch, a coffee table with empty snack bags and soju/beer cans, a big screen playing a lyrics video with over-the-top visuals, a disco ball casting light spots, a tambourine on the table, a song-selection remote, and mirrored wall panels reflecting the room. Slightly tacky, glowing, chaotic in the best way.
CAMERA / VISUAL AESTHETIC
Raw personal footage filmed by her friend on a phone, strong handheld vlog shake throughout.
Lighting shifts constantly with the neon cycle, causing exposure and color shifts across her face. Autofocus hunts between her face and the flashing screen behind her. Camera swings and dips with the friend's own laughter, mild motion blur during her more dramatic mic-swinging moments, visible digital noise in the dim room, colors slightly oversaturated from the neon wash.
No stabilization, no cinematic polish — it should feel like real footage that'll end up in a group chat.
00:00–00:05 — THE CONFIDENT INTRO
She grabs the mic with both hands, striking a mock-serious pop-star pose as the intro music starts.
She looks dead into the camera, completely deadpan and confident.
"Okay watch this. I'm actually good."
00:05–00:10 — STRONG START
The first line of the song hits and she nails it — eyes closed, hand on chest, fully committed to the performance.
The camera pushes in slightly, genuinely impressed, catching her hitting the note clean.
Her friend's voice off-camera: "Okay wait—?!"
00:10–00:15 — THE CRACK
The song hits a higher note and her voice visibly strains, cracking halfway through. Her eyes snap open in panic mid-note.
She tries to recover by belting harder, which makes it worse.
The camera shakes as the friend starts laughing, frame briefly clipping the ceiling.
00:15–00:20 — FULL COLLAPSE
She completely loses the melody, mumbling half the lyrics she doesn't know, gesturing wildly with the mic to compensate.
She turns away from the camera in embarrassment mid-line, then spins back in for a dramatic (bad) finish, hair flying.
The frame overshoots trying to follow her spin, briefly blurring.
00:20–00:25 — GIVING UP
She drops onto the couch mid-song, still holding the mic up weakly, mumbling the last few lines into the cushion instead of singing them.
The score screen pops up on the TV behind her with a visibly low number.
She peeks at the score, winces hard, and covers her face with a couch pillow.
00:25–00:30 — FINAL MOMENT
She lowers the pillow slowly, mic still limp in her other hand, and stares into the camera in mock devastation.
"...We're never speaking about this again."
Her friend, still laughing off-camera, zooms in too close on her defeated face — she weakly swats the lens away — and the footage cuts abruptly to black.
AUDIO
Natural location sound only:
Karaoke backing track playing from the room's speaker (muffled, roomy), her actual singing — strong at first, then cracking and falling apart — her friend's genuine off-camera laughter throughout, mic feedback crackle, couch cushion thud, tambourine jingling faintly when knocked, and handheld camera noise.
No added music. No narration. No artificial sound effects.
Spoken lines: "Okay watch this. I'm actually good." / "Okay wait—?!" (friend, off-camera) / "...We're never speaking about this again."
FINAL FEEL
Chaotic, glowing, late-night noraebang energy — the universal experience of confidently starting a karaoke song and immediately regretting every choice that led to that moment. Funny, cringe-in-a-good-way, genuinely unscripted.
No polished performance. No actual singing talent required — the comedy comes from the real vocal crack, real panic, and the gap between her confidence and her execution.

title: A Quiet Moment Alone
prompt:

OPERATOR LOCK: the camera is held by someone standing just inside the apartment
at the open sliding door, filming her casually through the doorway and stepping
half a step out later — it is a person's hands and it SHOWS: it drifts,
re-aims, reacts late, leans, and cuts her off at the frame edge. ANTI-POLISH
LOCK: NO stabilization, gimbal, drone, slow motion, dramatic lighting, cinematic
choreography, rack focus, lens flares, commercial color grading or polished
cinematography. NO music of any kind. The recording ENDS ABRUPTLY mid-motion, no
fade, no composed final frame.
CAPTURE: shot on an early smartphone — soft image detail, mild motion blur,
visible digital noise in the dim interior, imperfect white balance that shifts
as the camera moves from the room toward the doorway, slightly muted color,
natural compression, exposure hunting against the flat bright grey sky outside.
A small third-floor apartment balcony on a quiet residential street: chipped
concrete floor, a low painted railing, an air-conditioner unit, a folding
drying rack with two shirts on it, six or seven potted plants along the wall, a
plastic stool. Overcast afternoon, heavy still air before rain. Grade: flat,
grey-green, unglamorous — the texture of a forgotten personal recording, NOT a
film, NOT a commercial, NOT AI.

build, wearing an oversized faded grey t-shirt, black cotton shorts, and worn

consistent from first frame to last.

holds there on nothing.

title: Unboxing Old
prompt:
Create a 15-second ultra-realistic cinematic unboxing video filmed as if a real person is discovering something impossible.
SCENE:
A mysterious ancient wooden crate sits on a worn wooden table inside a dimly lit medieval-style room. The crate is reinforced with old iron bands, covered in scratches, dust, strange engraved symbols, and faintly glowing cracks. The camera is handheld in a realistic first-person unboxing POV, as if the person is filming the discovery with a modern smartphone.
0–3 seconds — THE UNBOXING:
The camera slowly moves closer to the crate. Two hands enter frame and carefully remove the rusty metal latches. The wooden lid creaks open. A subtle warm orange glow escapes from inside, illuminating the person's hands and the surrounding dust particles.
3–6 seconds — THE REVEAL:
Inside the crate is a tiny baby dragon, curled up asleep on a bed of dark velvet and straw. It looks completely realistic — detailed scales, tiny claws, leathery folded wings, expressive eyes, subtle breathing, warm skin tones, tiny horns, and realistic animal anatomy. The dragon slowly opens its eyes and blinks directly at the camera.
6–9 seconds — THE FIRE SNEEZE:
The baby dragon suddenly twitches its nose, looks confused, and lets out an adorable sneeze. A tiny burst of realistic orange fire shoots from its nostrils. The flame briefly illuminates its face and the inside of the crate. The person filming instinctively pulls the camera backward in surprise.
9–12 seconds — THE TRANSFORMATION:
The dragon becomes excited and begins growing rapidly. Its body expands naturally and seamlessly, scales shifting realistically as its wings unfold. Its wings become much larger, powerful, and detailed. It lets out a playful roar while rising out of the crate.
12–15 seconds — THE CRAZY PAYOFF:
The now larger young dragon suddenly spreads its wings and flies around the room, knocking loose dust from the ceiling. The camera follows it with realistic handheld movement as it circles overhead. It briefly lands on a wooden beam, looks directly into the camera, exhales a tiny stream of smoke, then launches toward an open window.
VISUAL STYLE:
Photorealistic fantasy creature, Hollywood blockbuster cinematography, physically accurate dragon movement, realistic scales and skin texture, detailed eyes, natural fire simulation, volumetric lighting, atmospheric dust, cinematic shadows, realistic handheld smartphone footage, shallow depth of field, subtle motion blur, high dynamic range, dramatic but believable lighting, premium VFX.
CAMERA:
First-person POV, handheld smartphone camera, natural human movement, occasional autofocus adjustment, realistic exposure changes when the fire appears, close-up macro detail during the reveal, wider tracking shot during the flight.
IMPORTANT:
The dragon must look photorealistic and physically believable, not cartoonish, not anime, not toy-like. Maintain consistent dragon appearance throughout the entire transformation. Realistic anatomy, realistic physics, seamless transformation, natural interaction with the environment.
AUDIO:
Wooden crate creaking, metal latch sounds, subtle room ambience, dragon breathing, tiny sneeze, realistic fire burst, surprised camera operator reaction, wing flaps, claws scraping wood, deep but youthful dragon roar, cinematic environmental sound. No background music.

title: Trash Balcony
prompt:
RAW HOME PHONE VIDEO. One continuous 30-second clip recorded on a current smartphone from a facing balcony. Amateur handheld, natural micro-shake, occasional clumsy pinch-zooms in and out. No film look, no cinematic grade, no grain recipe. Overcast gray daylight, peeling block facade, rust, smoke, wet concrete, cheap plastic. Trash metal blasting from the black speaker. Feels like a neighbor filmed it.
Characters
A big bald man with beard and mullet, balcony, grill, Jack Daniel's tap, blue inflatable pool, rubber ducks, speaker, railing and building. Man with receding hair with long sides, gold chain, black SLAYER tank, belly and seated posture.
TIMELINE
0-10s: [Handheld phone wide] The man sits dead-calm in the tiny blue kiddie pool, cigarette in his right hand, living like a king. Serious, unhurried, enjoying. Trash metal pounds. With his free left hand he reaches to the smoking grill, picks up a sausage, smells it, then puts it back exactly where it was. Steam rolls. The phone slowly zooms toward his face, then clumsily zooms back out. He never stands.
10-20s: [Handheld, lazy zoom] His large wife in a floral dress steps out the open door with an empty glass. She fills it from the Jack Daniel's tap with apple juice the same amber color as whiskey, and hands it to him. He takes a long swallow without getting up. She hikes the dress and climbs into the cramped pool with him. They splash. Ducks bob. He stays seated, still smoking, still unbothered. Camera wobbles in on the pour, then out to both of them.
20-30s: [Handheld widening, more shake as it gets worse] A black cat walks out the door and crosses the rusty railing. Only after the cat passes along the railing does the terrace start to crack: hairline fractures spread through the slab. The balcony slowly sags. The inflatable pool tilts; water sloshes over the rim. The couple slide with the tipping pool. The cat jumps out of frame. Concrete splits, railing twists, grill and speaker shift. The terrace gives way and they fall with the water as the clip ends.
AUDIO
Loud trash metal from the speaker the entire time. Grill sizzle, tap pour, splash, groaning metal, cracking concrete, rushing water. Distant courtyard noise. No dialogue. No extra score. No cinematic sound design.
STYLE & QUALITY
Looks like a real phone video from today: auto exposure, slightly crushed highlights, ordinary digital noise, real weight and water physics, wet skin and fabric, collapsing structure with coherent debris.

title: FPV Cheetah Hunt
prompt:
One CONTINUOUS FPV drone shot, no cuts, one unbroken take, EXTREME real-time speed. The footage NEVER reverses or plays backward. NO slow motion except one half-second beat at the reveal, then an instant snap back to full speed. Photoreal point-blank FPV framing. The camera flies LOW, at grass and knee height, its only altitude change one downward drop off the riverbank. NO ESCAPE, no fade to black — the take runs until time runs out, still inside the chaos.
CINEMATIC CAPTURE: real FPV drone footage — ultra-wide 14mm lens, barrel distortion, 180-degree shutter, heavy motion blur on fast pans, fine 35mm grain, lens flares off the low sun, dust and water hitting the lens. Golden-hour light under a bruised storm sky, one shaft of low gold raking the plain, a living savannah, herds and birds throughout. Grade: dry ochre and bleached gold, documentary contrast — the texture of a BBC nature documentary from a racing drone, NOT a game engine, NOT animation.
The shot opens ALREADY at full speed, skimming grass tips inches behind a sprinting cheetah at 110 km/h, claws throwing dirt at the lens. Ahead — seen ONLY from behind and flank, NEVER its face — an impala jinks hard right; the camera BANKS 90 degrees with it, tearing sideways through grass as guinea fowl burst around the lens. The impala zigzags; the camera snaps left, right, left with each cut, the cheetah's shoulder filling frame. Ahead a zebra herd grazes; the two tear into it and the herd EXPLODES — zebras rear, wheel and bolt in every direction, throwing a wall of dust. The camera stays LOW and threads THROUGH the stampede at knee height, swerving between hammering legs and striped bodies, dust raking the lens, then bursts out the far side back onto the cheetah's tail. Ahead a SHALLOW RIVER CHANNEL cuts the plain — muddy water, black mud. The impala plunges in; the camera drops VERTICALLY off the bank lip after it, out across the water, spray hitting the lens. THE ENTIRE CLIMAX HAPPENS HERE, IN THE WATER AND MUD — the channel never leaves frame. THE REVEAL: half-second slow motion — the cheetah at full stretch in its final lunge, low and flat over the shallows, claws out, seen from behind — then an INSTANT SNAP back to full speed. The paw hooks the flank at an angle; both crash sideways into the shallows, muddy water erupting, the camera driving THROUGH the splash, orbiting tight and low as they thrash, bodies soaked black. The jaws lock; the cheetah drags the kill through the mud, water streaming off its coat, the camera circling recklessly close. It plants its feet in the water over the body, flanks heaving with ragged open-mouthed panting, and lets rip a HIGH, PIERCING CHEETAH YOWL — a rasping chirp-scream breaking into a snarl and hiss, teeth bared, NOT a lion's roar. Vultures drop past the lens, the zebra herd stampedes on the far bank, the camera still arcing around the soaked, snarling cheetah as the runtime runs out mid-chaos.
Sound: a howling wall of grass-rush and wind pitching with every bank and drop, stampeding hooves, a driving score — dropping to one held breath of near-silence at the slow-motion reveal, then a MASSIVE concussive water impact, then sustained escalating chaos: thrashing water, ragged panting, hissing snarls, the piercing yowl, vulture wings, herd thunder, the score building to the final frame.
Global style lock: photoreal cinematic FPV; the camera stays low, the animals stay grounded, nothing rises into the sky; the climax escalates rather than resolves, no directed ending; the prey NEVER turns to face the predator or camera while running; EVERY background animal REACTS and keeps moving — nothing stands still as the chase passes; the river persists through the climax; no lion roar; no distortion, no subtitles, no watermarks.

title: Ancient Sword Palace Forbidden Reunion
prompt:
生成一支 25 秒、写实电影质感、原生同步中文对白的双人古装史诗对话短片。画幅为宽银幕 2.39:1，24fps 观感，轻微胶片颗粒，整体具有东方史诗武侠电影气质：秦汉古意、极简宫殿、大片朱红帷幕、黑色石地、金色烛火、冷白天光从高处斜落。画面庄严、克制、留白充足，色彩以深红、黑、金、灰白为主，不要现代物品，不要商业广告感。全片不出现任何第三个人物。
【人物一致性】
男人：42 岁左右的东亚男性，秦宫武士或无名刺客，脸型清瘦，眉骨分明，眼神沉静如铁，皮肤略粗糙，唇线紧。黑发束冠，穿黑色宽领古代长袍，只拍胸部以上，衣料厚重、无现代纹样。声音低沉、平稳、克制，语速慢，每个字像压在胸腔里。
女人：38 岁左右的东亚女性，前朝剑客或宫中旧友，面容冷静，眼神清亮而压抑，黑发高束，鬓边一缕碎发，穿深红色古代衣袍，只拍胸部以上。声音清冷、柔韧，前半段平静，后半段出现难以压住的颤音。
两人始终保持相同面孔、年龄、服装、发型和站位，不出现面部漂移、服装变化或年龄变化。人物不得模仿任何现实演员或公众人物。男人位于空间左侧，女人位于空间右侧，相距约一米，遵守 180 度轴线，视线始终准确对接。
【镜头一｜0.0—4.5 秒】
85mm 人像镜头，男人胸部以上近景，三分之二侧脸朝向画面右侧。背景是虚化的巨大朱红帷幕和一排金色烛火，景深极浅。摄影机近乎固定，只保留非常轻微的空气流动感。
男人低垂眼帘，右手在画面下缘轻轻按住剑柄，但不拔剑。他抬眼看向女人，眉心没有明显皱起，却有极强压迫感。声音低而慢：
"你若再往前一步，我便不能留你。"
说到"不能"时，他的下颌轻微收紧；说到"留你"时，眼神短暂变软，又立即恢复冷静。硬切。
【镜头二｜4.5—10.5 秒】
切到女人越肩近景。男人的肩膀和黑色衣领作为模糊前景，占据画面左侧边缘。女人位于画面中央偏右，胸部以上构图，深红衣袍与背后朱红帷幕形成压迫性的色块。镜头固定，烛火在她眼中微微颤动。
女人没有后退。她先看向男人按剑的手，再抬眼看回他的眼睛。嘴唇轻轻压紧，呼吸很浅。她说：
"你留过我一次。"
停顿半秒，声音更轻，却更锋利：
"那一次，我用了十年才明白，是怜悯，不是情。"
说到"怜悯"时，她的眼睑轻微收紧；说到"不是情"时，嘴角几乎不可见地向下沉。硬切。
【镜头三｜10.5—16.0 秒】
回到男人近景，比第一镜更近，只到肩膀和脸。85mm，背景朱红帷幕完全虚化，黑色石地的冷光从下方轻轻反到脸上。摄影机做几乎察觉不到的缓慢推近。
男人的眼神第一次出现裂缝。眉毛内侧微微下压，喉结完成一次克制吞咽，嘴唇先闭紧再缓慢分开。他没有立刻反驳，而是沉默半秒后低声说：
"我若说那不是怜悯，你会信吗？"
说完后他仍看着她，但眼底有一瞬间的疲惫。不要流泪，不要低头痛哭。硬切。
【镜头四｜16.0—22.0 秒】
女人极近景，脸占据画面大部分，但不要变形。背景只剩模糊的红、黑、金三种色块。她的眼睛微微睁大，像被这句话击中，却强迫自己保持平静。
她的眉毛内侧轻微上扬，眼眶出现湿润反光，但不要落泪。她缓慢吸气，声音开始有细微颤动：
"我信不信，已经不重要了。"
停顿极短，她看向男人的眼睛，语气由柔变冷：
"天下要你活着，可我只想问一句。"
她的嘴唇轻轻发抖，最后一句压得很低：
"你有没有一刻，想跟我走？"
硬切。
【镜头五｜22.0—25.0 秒】
双人胸部以上中近景，不出现全身。两人面对面站在大殿朱红帷幕之间，男人在画面左侧，女人位于空间右侧，中间隔着一束冷白天光。画面稳定、对称、庄严，只有帷幕被风轻轻推动。
男人没有回答。女人也没有动。男人按在剑柄上的手指慢慢松开半寸，却仍没有离开剑。女人看见这个动作，眼神里的冷意短暂崩开，露出一点迟来的悲伤。
男人终于低声说：
"想过。"
停顿半秒。
"所以更不能走。"
最后保持两人对视 0.4 秒，直接结束，不淡出。
【声音设计】
原生生成中文对白，严格区分两位说话者，口型与每个音节准确同步。男人声音低沉、平稳、压抑，像每句话都经过长久克制；女人声音清冷、柔韧，后段出现细小颤音，但不要哭喊。保留真实换气、吞咽、厚重衣料轻微摩擦、烛火燃烧声、空旷宫殿混响和帷幕被风推动的低声。不要背景音乐，不要旁白，不要字幕，不要夸张兵器音效。
【影像限制】
不要全身镜头，不要远景，不要大规模打斗，不要飞天动作，不要慢动作展示武打。不要字幕、不要任何可读文字、不要水印、不要 Logo。不要新增第三个人物，不要切换场景，不要改变服装和发型，不要面孔漂移，不要美颜磨皮，不要现代物品，不要夸张肢体动作，不要持续喊叫，不要快速环绕镜头，不要商业广告灯光，不要异常牙齿、嘴唇粘连、口型错位、目光漂移或不自然流泪。
【核心要求】
这是一场刺杀前被天下大义压住的旧情对话，画面的力量来自红黑金色块中的克制凝视、未拔出的剑，以及两个人终于承认却无法选择的遗憾。

Realistic 30-second handheld Hong Kong lifestyle vlog. A young adult Hong Kong woman with a sweet, modern look and casual outfit. Keep her face and identity consistent. Natural Hong Kong Cantonese with accurate lip sync only. No Mandarin or English.
Shot by a friend on a smartphone with natural handheld shake, casual framing and spontaneous movement. Authentic everyday vlog.
0–6s: She leaves an apartment, checks her phone and smiles:「早晨呀，今日帶你哋睇下我平時點過一日。」
6–13s: She walks into a cha chaan teng, orders iced milk tea and breakfast:「呢間我成日嚟㗎，奶茶幾正。」

Realistic people, natural daylight and Hong Kong atmosphere. No subtitles, text, logos, transitions, exaggerated acting or identity changes.

title: Korea 15Y Ago
prompt:
Create a 30-second, 1080p ultra-realistic personal home-video showing an ordinary summer morning in the life of a young Korean woman. No reference image.
MAIN SUBJECT
Young Korean woman in her early 20s, naturally pretty, realistic skin texture, minimal makeup and relaxed personality.
Long black wavy hair loosely tied into a messy side ponytail with a few loose strands around her face. Wearing a fitted white short top, loose light-blue pajama-style pants, black sneakers and a simple silver necklace.
Maintain the same face, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions and overall appearance throughout the entire video.
SETTING
A quiet older Seoul residential neighborhood during a warm summer morning. Small houses, concrete stairs, narrow alleys, potted plants, bicycles, old walls, overhead wires, neighborhood taps and large leafy trees.
Everything feels lived-in, ordinary and peaceful.
CAMERA / VISUAL AESTHETIC
Raw personal footage recorded by a friend on an early-2000s consumer DV camcorder.
Strong handheld shake, slightly crooked framing, autofocus hunting, faded colors, soft digital detail, exposure shifts, occasional motion blur, mild digital noise and imperfect zooms.
No stabilization, drone footage or polished commercial cinematography.
— OUTSIDE HER HOME
She sits on the concrete steps outside her house looking slightly sleepy.
She notices the public water tap beside the entrance, gets up and walks toward it.
She turns the tap on and splashes cool water onto her face with both hands.
Water droplets remain visible on her skin as she looks toward the camera and smiles.
She says:
"Way too hot already."
— MORNING ROUTINE
She wipes her face with a small towel and ties her messy ponytail a little tighter.
She takes a sip from a cold bottled drink sitting beside the tap.
The camera zooms awkwardly toward her wet face, briefly loses focus, then snaps back.
She laughs at the camera.
— WALK THROUGH THE LANE
She grabs a small reusable shopping bag and starts walking down the narrow street.
She passes a neighbor sweeping outside their home and gives them a cheerful morning greeting.
A bicycle rolls past her and she steps aside, laughing as the camera nearly misses the moment.
— SMALL BREAKFAST STOP
She reaches a tiny neighborhood bakery and looks through the window.
She buys a warm pastry, steps outside and immediately takes a bite.
She smiles with genuine satisfaction and holds the pastry toward the camera.
— UNEXPECTED FRIEND
Her friend suddenly appears at the end of the alley and calls her.
She turns around, waves excitedly and walks toward them.
They briefly chat while standing beside a row of bicycles, then start walking together down the lane.
— FINAL MOMENT
They reach a large tree casting shade across the street.
She sits on a low concrete wall, finishes her pastry and looks peacefully down the quiet neighborhood.
Her friend points the camera toward her.
She notices and says:
"Okay, that's enough filming."
She reaches toward the lens with her hand.
The image becomes blurry as her fingers cover the camera.
The recording abruptly cuts to black.
AUDIO
Natural location sound only: running water, birds, summer insects, footsteps, bicycle bells, distant scooters, sweeping sounds, bakery ambience, quiet conversations and subtle camcorder handling noise.
No music. No narration. No artificial sound effects.
Only the two spoken lines specified above.
FINAL FEEL
The entire video should feel like a real forgotten summer morning recording from the early 2000s.
Casual, feminine, warm, nostalgic and slightly funny.
No dramatic events, no model poses, no polished commercial shots.
The realism should come from wet skin, real water droplets, imperfect handheld footage, ordinary Korean streets, natural expressions and tiny everyday interactions.

title: Forgotten Summer Tape Camcorder Aesthetic

The trick isn't the grain or the shake. It's writing a version of the day where the camera is furniture, not a costar.

Subject: Person from (Image1). Face and hairstyle must match (Image1) completely do not transform into a different person. Ignore the outfit, gym, backpack, pose, background, and bottom text from Image1. Even if image quality is rough, facial features must remain clearly defined. Same woman throughout, late 20s, curly dark ponytail that gets messier as the night goes on.
She is with ONE friend the entire video. Friend is a different real person (not Image1): mid-20s American woman, straight dirty-blonde hair, denim jacket, jeans, not a model. Friend stays the same face/outfit logic all night. She leans into the selfie, talks over her, does not pose.
Outfit changes by cut (normal going-out clothes, not luxury): black tank + jeans + gold hoops at home; same plus a cheap black jacket in the street; later jacket zipped, smeared lip gloss, tired face. White sneakers, small black shoulder bag. No heels, no sequins, no designer bags.
16:9 landscape. Front-facing selfie the entire time. She never puts the phone down. No rear camera, no propped shots, no tripod, no friend holding the camera. Entire video has an old iPhone low-quality everyday-vlog look. Constant heavy noise and compression artifacts throughout.
Setting: Real Saturday night in Columbus, Ohio. Mid-size Midwest US city, brick bar street, cheap bars, a small club, a late-night taco counter, a normal Uber. No landmarks, no skyline money shot. No legible text/signage/branding anywhere in frame.
Timeline:
0–3s: Bedroom selfie, arm's length, she finishes lipstick, friend on the bed behind her, talking to camera: "okay we're going out, I wasn't gonna but whatever." Friend: "you were gonna."
3–6s: Bathroom selfie, both in the mirror behind the phone, she tugs her top, friend laughs, they grab jackets.
6–9s: Walking selfie on a packed brick bar street, friend beside her in frame, she says: "this is it, it's already chaos." Friend looks away at a group of guys.
9–12s: Bar selfie, both holding cheap drinks, they clink, she talks into the mic: "we just got here and it's packed." Friend yells something unintelligible.
12–15s: Club-bathroom-line selfie, harsh fluorescent, both of them, she yells: "we can't even get in the bathroom." Friend rolls her eyes.
15–18s: Tiny club selfie, cheap lights, they dance, friend bumps the phone, she laughs, not performing.
18–21s: Outside 3am selfie, jackets on, cold, hair messy, she says: "I need food immediately." Friend: "tacos. now."
21–24s: Taco counter selfie, fluorescent, they eat with both hands, she talks with her mouth half full: "best decision of the night." Friend nods hard.
24–27s: Uber back-seat selfie, both tired, city lights on the window, she leans in: "don't talk to me until tomorrow." Friend already on her phone.
27–30s: Apartment hallway selfie, keys, shoes kicked off, both on the floor, wrecked smiles: "we're dead. bye," freeze on final frame.
Camera: Loose 1–1.5s cuts stacked inside those windows. Old iPhone, 16:9, standard 1x front camera (no distortion, standard field of view), natural handheld shake the whole time, mixed night lighting: warm cheap bar tungsten, blown club lights, cold street, ugly taco fluorescent, off white balance.
Sound: No BGM. Ambient only (street chatter, glasses, muffled bass from a door, bathroom fan, kitchen extractor, car rattle). Natural talking voice with slight handheld mic distortion. They talk over each other. Background American voices.
Style: Unedited low-quality phone vlog look. No color grading, no film look, no cinematic look, no beauty filter, no CG texture. No fisheye/ultra-wide (0.5x)/action-cam look, no barrel distortion, no vignette, no black lens-round at frame edges, flat standard field of view, frame filled edge to edge. Real skin texture maintained (pores, flyaway hairs, shiny T-zone, smeared makeup by the end). No on-screen text. No luxury nightlife, no bottle service, no rooftop, no Miami, no NYC.

title: Summer Evening Vlog Baddie
prompt:
Create a 30-second, 1080p ultra-realistic personal home-video showing an ordinary summer evening in the life of a young Korean woman. No reference image.
MAIN SUBJECT
Young Korean woman in her early 20s, naturally pretty, realistic skin texture, minimal makeup, relaxed and approachable personality.
Long black hair loosely tied into a messy side ponytail with a few loose strands around her face. Wearing a fitted pastel-blue short top, loose cream pajama-style pants, black sneakers and a simple silver necklace.
Maintain the same face, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions and overall appearance throughout the entire video.
SETTING
A quiet older Seoul residential neighborhood during a warm summer evening. Narrow concrete lanes, small houses, potted plants, bicycles, old walls, utility poles, overhead wires, a tiny neighborhood bakery, a public water tap and large leafy trees casting shadows across the street.
Everything should feel lived-in, ordinary and peaceful. No tourist attractions, advertisements, recognizable brands or commercial activity.
CAMERA / VISUAL AESTHETIC
Raw personal footage casually recorded by a friend on an early-2000s consumer DV camcorder.
Strong handheld shake, imperfect framing, autofocus hunting, exposure shifts, occasional motion blur, faded colors, soft digital detail, mild noise, accidental zooms and natural camera imperfections.
No stabilization, drone footage, gimbal movement, dramatic lighting or polished commercial cinematography.
— OUTSIDE THE HOUSE
She steps outside carrying a small reusable shopping bag. She locks the door, adjusts her messy ponytail and looks toward the camera with a relaxed smile.
A light summer breeze moves her hair as she starts walking down the lane.
— BAKERY STOP
She reaches a tiny neighborhood bakery and buys a warm pastry.
She steps outside, takes her first bite and immediately smiles because it tastes good.
She notices her friend filming and holds the pastry toward the camera playfully before taking another bite.
— WALKING HOME
She continues down the narrow street while eating.
A neighborhood cat follows her for a few steps. She notices it, crouches down and gently pets it.
The cat walks away and she laughs before continuing.
— SMALL ACCIDENT
She walks beneath a large tree when a few leaves fall onto her hair.
She stops, looks confused, then realizes what happened and laughs.
She brushes the leaves away while her friend zooms awkwardly toward her face.
She looks directly into the camera and says:
"Seriously?"
— QUIET MOMENT
She reaches a low concrete wall beside the street and sits down for a moment.
She finishes the pastry while watching bicycles and neighbors passing through the lane.
A gentle breeze moves her hair. She casually fixes her ponytail and looks around peacefully.
— FINAL MOMENT
She stands up and continues walking home.
After a few steps, she turns back toward the camera with a small playful smile and says:
"Come on."
She keeps walking down the sunny lane while the camera follows behind.
She disappears around the corner and the recording abruptly cuts to black.
AUDIO
Natural location sound only: birds, summer insects, footsteps, bicycle bells, distant scooters, leaves moving in the breeze, bakery sounds, neighborhood conversations and subtle camera-handling noise.
No music. No narration. No artificial sound effects.
Only the two spoken lines specified above.
FINAL FEEL
The entire video should feel like a forgotten summer recording from the early 2000s.
Warm, feminine, casual, slightly playful, intimate and nostalgic.
No dramatic events, no exaggerated acting, no model poses and no polished cinematic shots.
The realism should come from ordinary surroundings, natural expressions, small accidents, realistic environmental movement and imperfect camcorder operation.

title: Apocalypse Train One Take
prompt:
基础概括： 30秒写实末日科幻一镜到底，16:9。摄影机始终位于行驶中的列车车厢内，以35mm、乘客坐姿眼高沿过道极缓慢 Track Forward 约1.5米，全程无剪辑、无跳帧、无转向窗外。画面左侧55%固定为车窗与不断变化的世界，右侧45%固定为复古未来车厢；唯一女乘客始终坐在右侧靠窗座位，外貌、服装、座位和身体方向全程不变，只通过视线、呼吸、手部和坐姿变化回应窗外末日景象。
空间与运动锁定： 右侧深绿色座椅、木饰面、黄铜扶手、行李架和暖色顶灯始终保持相同结构，不随时空变形。窗框位置固定，玻璃始终存在真实反射与污痕。列车持续向前高速行驶，窗外保持三层视差：近景飞速掠过，中景稳定横移，远景缓慢移动；所有时代转换都由覆盖整面车窗的天气、黑暗或强光自然衔接。
整体声音与光影： 无背景音乐、无对白。连续铁轨节奏、车轮低频轰鸣、车厢轻微震动和玻璃颤响贯穿全片，作为时空连续性锚点；冰雪冲击、沙砾刮窗、洪水雷鸣、灰烬风声和宇宙低频脉冲依次叠入。车内暖黄顶灯始终不灭，窗外的冷蓝、沙黄、暴雨青灰、灰烬暗红与黑洞白金光依次扫过乘客面部、座椅和黄铜边缘，光色改变但车厢材质不改变。
0-4秒｜雨夜启程
第一帧可清晰重建：左侧车窗外是现代城市废弃站台，暴雨斜落，空荡站棚和故障灯向画面后方滑去；右侧女乘客三分之二侧身坐着，身体朝车头，脸转向左侧车窗，双手松放在膝前。摄影机开始极缓慢前移。她神情疲惫平静，目光跟随站台末端最后一盏灯。雨滴在玻璃上向后拉成长线，站台进入黑暗隧道。
4-9秒｜冰川崩塌
隧道黑暗中，窗上雨水迅速凝成冰晶；列车驶出时，左侧出现辽阔冰封峡谷，巨大冰川在远处断裂，雪崩沿山壁追向轨道。冷蓝强光扫进车厢，乘客先停止眨眼，随后短促吸气，右手抓紧座椅边缘，身体因列车震动轻微后靠。雪浪逼近并覆盖整面车窗，玻璃只产生受压震颤，不碎裂。
9-14秒｜沙暴废土
覆盖车窗的白色雪雾逐渐变成黄褐色尘暴。沙尘退开，窗外已是炽热废土：倾斜的输电塔、半埋铁轨和废弃公路标志高速掠过，远处城市只剩风化轮廓。沙砾持续刮擦玻璃。乘客仍握住座椅，肩膀绷紧；她稍微向窗边倾身，目光越过近处废墟寻找生命迹象，发现什么都没有后，嘴唇缓慢抿紧。
14-19秒｜洪水都市
浓沙再次吞没车窗，一道白色闪电从沙幕中划过；闪光退去，沙砾声无缝转为暴雨。列车冲上高架轨道，窗外是被洪水淹没的现代巨城，水面接近摩天楼中层，车辆和屋顶残骸随黑色水流旋转，远处闪电照亮倾斜建筑。青灰水光在车厢内晃动。乘客松开座椅，左手缓慢抬起，指尖贴住冰冷玻璃；眼睛跟随水中漂过的一只空玩具船，眼眶开始湿润但不落泪。
19-24秒｜灰烬死城
列车穿过一段被洪水淹没的桥下阴影，窗外短暂全黑；驶出阴影后进入无声的核冬天废城。天空暗红，灰烬像雪一样横向飞过，坍塌高楼、烧焦森林和远处微弱火线缓慢后退，没有尸体、没有活人。铁轨声变得空旷沉重。乘客贴在玻璃上的手指逐渐蜷缩，再慢慢收回胸前；她喉咙吞咽一次，眼神从恐惧转为悲伤，第一滴泪无声滑过脸颊。
24-28秒｜驶出世界
大片灰烬彻底遮住窗外，车厢灯连续轻闪两次，但空间结构不变。灰烬旋转速度越来越慢，逐渐化为宇宙星尘；窗外地面消失，列车沿一条悬浮发光轨道驶入深空，巨大黑洞位于远方，白金色吸积盘缓慢旋转。列车重力保持稳定。乘客发现自己仍能呼吸后，抓住衣襟的手一点点松开，重新转向窗外，泪痕保留，脸上不再只有恐惧，而是安静的震撼与接受。
28-30秒｜终点未知
摄影机停止前移，保持构图。黑洞的弧形白光掠过车窗，在乘客瞳孔、湿润脸颊和黄铜扶手上留下移动高光。铁轨节奏逐渐与低沉宇宙脉冲重合。她坐直身体，目光稳定地望向黑洞，没有后退；窗玻璃中同时保留她的淡淡倒影与远方光环。最后1.5秒持续向黑洞行驶，不揭示终点，画面自然切黑。
人物表演控制： 情绪路径为疲惫麻木、骤然警觉、寻找生机、目睹文明消失后的悲伤、面对终极未知的接受。所有反应必须由窗外事件触发并延迟半拍；不尖叫、不站起、不大幅挥手。动作锚点依次为双手放松、抓紧座椅、身体前倾、指尖触窗、收手护住胸口、最终松开并坐直。
负面约束： 不剪辑、不瞬移、不改变镜头轴线和左右构图；车厢、窗框、座椅、灯具、乘客脸部与服装全程一致。窗外转换必须经过完整遮挡，不生硬闪切；保持高速视差，不生成静态背景贴图。不要新增乘客、重复人物、车窗破裂、物体穿透玻璃、失重漂浮、怪物、尸体、血腥、夸张爆炸、过度镜头抖动、字幕、水印和背景音乐。

title: Motocross Mud Rain Race
prompt:
Style: Premium cinematic motocross racing, gritty realism, extreme weather, heavy rain, deep mud, dramatic natural lighting, high energy. Duration: 30 seconds.
[0–5s] — The Veteran
Extreme close-up of the veteran rider’s mud-covered full-face helmet and tinted goggles, face completely hidden. Slow camera push-in as rain streams across the visor and mud sticks to the helmet. Subtle breathing and engine vibration. Shallow depth of field, realistic rain droplets and lens moisture.
[5–10s] — The Challenger
Cut to the second rider from a low side angle. Aggressive helmet design, covered in fresh mud. He leans forward and blips the throttle as the rear tire spins slightly, throwing wet dirt. Camera tracks smoothly beside the bike.
[10–15s] — Tension Before Launch
Wide establishing shot of the muddy starting gate under a dark stormy sky. Deep ruts, puddles, rain mist and reflective wet surfaces. Both riders hold position as engines grow louder. Brief close-ups of gripping gloves, throttle movement and spinning wheels.
[15–20s] — Explosive Launch
The gate slams down. Both riders launch violently forward. Low camera near the ground captures tires digging into mud and blasting water toward the lens. One rider lifts into a controlled wheelie. Brief slow motion as mud explodes through the air, then return to full speed.
[20–25s] — First Corner
Dynamic tracking shot alongside the riders as they attack the first muddy turn. Bikes slide naturally through deep ruts, suspension compresses, and thick mud sprays from the rear tires. Camera movement feels fast, physical and immersive.
[25–30s] — Into the Storm
Low rear tracking shot as the riders accelerate away, battling for position. Headlights glow through heavy rain and atmospheric mist. One rider edges ahead toward the next jump. Finish with a dramatic wide shot and brief slow-motion mud spray.
Cinematic Direction: Consistent riders, helmets, motorcycles and environment throughout. Realistic physics, natural motion blur, shallow depth of field, volumetric rain, subtle lens splashes, dramatic contrast, immersive camera choreography, authentic motocross movement. No unnecessary cuts, no exaggerated CGI effects.
Audio: Thunder, heavy rainfall, engine idle, throttle blips, rising RPM, gate slam, tire spin, mud impacts and powerful engine roar, synchronized naturally with the action.

【镜头四｜24.2–30.0s｜巅峰收尾·悲剧封神】

程蝶衣默然失神、低声呢喃收尾，满是绝望孤绝：“我本是女娇娥，又不是男儿郎……终究是我错了。”

3. 环境音：旧戏楼轻微空荡底噪、细碎风声、远处隐约戏韵余响，静谧清冷，烘托温柔破碎、宿命悲凉的极致氛围。
4. 永久禁止：BGM、配乐、旁白、戏剧音效、人声混响、特效音，纯双人对白+极简环境音，高级干净、氛围感纯粹厚重。
六、全局避坑黑名单（零BUG执行）

七、核心主旨
本片核心张力：戏是一生执念，人是一世虚妄。 程蝶衣以戏为命、从一而终，疯魔半生、执念一生；段小楼入世清醒、随遇而安，分得虚实、活得世俗。一个活成戏里忠贞虞姬，一个终究是凡间俗世霸王，半生纠缠、终身错位，是华语影史最极致、最意难平的宿命悲剧。
