title: Wrong Turn Station Encounter
prompt:
Ultra-realistic spontaneous vertical iPhone vacation video filmed during a bright summer afternoon in Japan.
FORMAT: Native vertical iPhone recording, 3:4 portrait orientation for the entire video. Never switch to landscape.
Use the provided reference image as the ONLY visual reference for the main woman. Keep her exact facial identity, hairstyle, skin tone, facial proportions, body proportions, and overall appearance consistent throughout the video. Do not beautify or redesign her.
The footage must look like a real vacation video casually recorded by a friend. No cinematic filmmaking, no staged acting, no influencer posing.
0–3 seconds
The video begins inside a small Japanese train station.
The group has just arrived and is walking toward the exit. The main woman confidently walks in the wrong direction.
A friend behind the camera says naturally, “Wrong way!”
She stops, looks back and laughs.
She replies, “Oh my god, seriously?”
The camera quickly turns toward her with natural handheld movement while a train passes in the background.
3–6 seconds
The group walks through a quiet residential street filled with small Japanese houses, greenery and utility poles.
The main woman is eating a small local snack while walking.
A friend asks, “Is it good?”
She takes another bite and casually says, “Actually, yeah.”
She notices the camera and gives a small laugh before continuing to walk.
The camera briefly gets too close and then naturally moves back.
6–9 seconds
The group reaches a small local summer festival.
There are simple food stalls, people eating, children playing and locals moving naturally through the area.
The main woman tries a small festival game and misses completely.
She looks at her friend and says, “That was so bad.”
Her friend laughs and replies, “You didn't even try.”
She starts laughing while the camera shakes slightly because the person filming is laughing too.
9–12 seconds
The group leaves the festival and walks along a shaded path surrounded by trees.
The main woman walks ahead and suddenly turns around.
She says, “Come on, hurry up!”
One friend answers from behind, “We're coming!”
She starts walking backward while talking, then notices the uneven path and quickly turns around.
Everyone laughs naturally.
12–15 seconds
The group reaches the top of a small hill overlooking an ordinary Japanese town.
There are rooftops, trees and distant mountains rather than a perfect tourist viewpoint.
The main woman looks at the view for a moment.
A friend hands her the unfinished snack from earlier and says, “You forgot this.”
She looks at it and laughs.
She replies, “I've been carrying this all day.”
Everyone laughs naturally.
The camera stays on the group for another second before cutting naturally.
CAMERA REALISM
Authentic iPhone home-video footage.
Natural handheld movement with imperfect framing, realistic walking shake, autofocus adjustments, automatic exposure changes, smartphone HDR, subtle sharpening, realistic motion blur, slight rolling shutter, occasional accidental cropping, natural lens flare and small exposure fluctuations.
The camera operator behaves like a real friend, not a professional videographer.
The camera sometimes reacts slightly late to events and occasionally points too high, too low or too close.
ENVIRONMENT
Believable Japanese summer neighborhood with a small train station, traditional houses, narrow streets, greenery, vending machines, utility poles, overhead wires, bicycles, local shops, summer festival stalls, pedestrians and distant mountains.
Everything should feel lived-in and ordinary.
HUMAN REALISM
The main woman remains visually identical to the reference.
Natural blinking, eye movement, breathing, walking, laughter and facial expressions.
Friends should behave naturally and should not constantly look at the camera.
Background people must have different faces, clothing and movements.
No duplicated people or synchronized crowd behavior.
AUDIO
Authentic iPhone microphone recording with train sounds, footsteps, distant conversations, birds, insects, wind, festival ambience, children, food-stall sounds, occasional traffic and natural laughter.
Dialogue should sound casual and spontaneous, with natural pauses and imperfect timing.

title: If You Think Ai Is Not There
prompt:
Handheld digital camcorder aesthetic, landscape framing.
A gorgeous fitness and food influencer films herself by hand in selfie-cam and first-person style while cooking a late-night high-protein meal after training and a shower.
Keep realistic hand shake, slightly crooked framing, autofocus briefly hunting between her face and the food, awkward zoom-ins onto the pan, occasional motion blur, brief lens steam-up over the hot pan that clears naturally, and small framing mistakes where her face or the pan edge slips out of frame.
Mix handheld selfie footage with a few fixed external shots.
Important: never show her placing, adjusting, or setting up a camera.
When switching from handheld footage to a fixed external angle, use a clean jump cut as if the camera had already been positioned before the shot began.
The camera itself must never appear on screen or in the window reflection.
LOOK:
Warm late-night kitchen light.
A single warm pendant over the counter, cool blue night visible through the window behind her, under-cabinet strip light glowing on the backsplash.
Slight camcorder softness, faint noise in the shadows, mild bloom on the pendant.
Food realism is the core of the look: real sizzle with fine oil spatter, steam rising and curling from the pan, honest food textures with sear marks and glistening surfaces, knife cuts that separate cleanly, droplets on rinsed vegetables.
Realistic skin texture, fresh-from-the-shower glow, clean dewy skin, realistic skin tones.
STYLE:
A realistic late-night what-I-eat-after-training vlog.
The tone is relaxed, hungry, funny, quietly confident, and natural, talking to the lens like a friend while her hands keep working.
She is clearly attractive and charismatic, but the video must feel like a believable self-recorded kitchen vlog, not a food commercial.
Fast clean jump cuts, strong continuity, natural body language, real kitchen sounds, sizzle, chopping, no awkward dead moments.
CHARACTER:
The woman in the reference image. Her face, features, skin tone, body, and clothing must match the reference image exactly in every shot — she wears exactly what she is wearing in the reference image. Do not restyle, beautify, or alter her in any way beyond the reference.
The one addition: a soft white towel wrapped around her head like a turban, as if she just stepped out of the shower. The towel stays neatly wrapped for the whole video. A few small damp strands of hair may peek out at the hairline and neck.
Minimal or no makeup, fresh clean post-shower look.
A small kitchen towel over one shoulder for most of the video.
SETTING:
A small warm real apartment kitchen at night.
Wooden counter with knife marks, a gas hob with one cast-iron pan, a cutting board with chicken breast and vegetables, a bowl of cooked rice, a bottle of olive oil, salt in a small dish, a fridge with magnets and photos, dishes drying on a rack, dark window over the sink reflecting the warm kitchen.
Lived-in and slightly cluttered.
No other people, no pets.
IMPORTANT CONTINUITY RULES:
The same woman from the reference image must remain fully consistent in every shot.
No face changes, no outfit changes, no body changes.
The head towel stays wrapped in the same position in every shot — it never unwraps, falls, changes color, or disappears.
The meal progresses in one direction only: raw ingredients, then chopping, then searing, then plating, then eating, and never reverses or regenerates.
Food already cooked never becomes raw again.
Hands and knife are the top priority: five fingers always, correct knife grip with curled guiding fingers, clean cuts, the knife never bends and never passes through her hand.
The pan, board, oil bottle and rice bowl stay in the same positions.
Steam and sizzle must behave with real physics.
No extra people, including in the dark window reflection, and the reflection never shows a camera.
No duplicated limbs.
No camera visible.
No camera setup shown.
Keep her matching the reference image, warm, and photogenic in every shot.
STORYBOARD:
30 seconds total, 10 cuts.
(~3s, arm's-length selfie)
She leans on the counter, towel wrapped on her head, clearly fresh from the shower after training, and grins tiredly at the lens.
Dialogue:
"Trained late. Showered. Starving. Let's cook."
(~3s, handheld pan across the counter and back to her)
The camera drifts across the board with raw chicken and vegetables, the pan, the rice bowl, then back up to her face.
Dialogue:
"Ten minute meal. Watch."
(~3s, fixed external medium shot from across the counter)
Jump cut.
She is already chopping a red pepper with quick confident cuts, guiding fingers curled, pieces falling evenly.
No camera setup shown.
No dialogue, just the knife on the board.
(~3s, same fixed shot)
She slices the chicken breast into strips, seasons it from the salt dish with a high pinch, and rubs it in with her fingertips.
Dialogue:
"Protein first. Always."
(~3s, tight handheld first-person shot over the pan)
Oil shimmering, she lays the chicken strips in one by one and they hit with a loud real sizzle, fine spatter, steam rising into the lens which fogs for a beat and clears.
No dialogue, just the sizzle.
(~3s, handheld selfie while the pan sizzles behind her)
She turns the camera on herself, fanning steam away from her face, laughing, one hand briefly steadying the head towel.
Dialogue:
"The smell. You have no idea."
(~3s, tight handheld close-up of the pan)
She flips the strips with tongs, showing deep golden sear marks, tosses in the peppers, and shakes the pan once so everything jumps and resettles.
Dialogue:
"That colour? That's the whole point."
(~3s, fixed external shot)
Jump cut.
She plates it: rice pressed from the bowl, chicken and peppers over the top, a last drizzle of olive oil in a thin ribbon, and she wipes the plate rim with the towel like a chef, then smirks at her own seriousness.
Dialogue:
"Yes, I wiped the rim. Let me live."
(~3s, tight handheld close-up)
First fork bite, steam still coming off it, she chews, closes her eyes for a beat and nods slowly.
Dialogue:
"Ten minutes. That's it. Ridiculous."
(~3s, arm's-length selfie ending)
Plate in one hand, camera in the other, she backs out of the kitchen toward the sofa, flicking the kitchen light off with her elbow.
Dialogue:
"Okay. Eating. Good night."
FINAL INSTRUCTION:
The result must feel like a real self-recorded late-night cooking vlog by an athlete who actually cooks, filmed right after her shower.
The highest priorities are matching the reference image exactly, correct hands and knife work at close range, one-directional cooking progression that never reverses, real sizzle, steam and food texture, the head towel staying consistently wrapped, honest warm kitchen light against the dark window, and subtle imperfection.
Keep it warm, hungry, and real.
Not a food commercial, not overhead recipe content, not stiff.

title: Creating Hand-Drawn Vfx That Morphs Across Your
prompt:
15-second, 16:9 horizontal video. A fusion of live-action footage inside a dark cozy bedroom and hand-drawn glowing animation.
A lived-in bedroom illuminated only by a warm bedside lamp, faint fairy lights, and the glow of a laptop screen. Clothes, books, cables, cups, and everyday objects remain naturally scattered around the room. The footage feels like spontaneous one-handed smartphone recording, with subtle hand shake, low-light sensor noise, occasional focus hunting, motion blur, rolling exposure shifts, imperfect framing, and natural auto-exposure fluctuations.
0–3 seconds: A finger touches the surface of a glass of water on the desk. A thin glowing turquoise hand-drawn line leaks out from beneath the fingertip and crawls across the desk like liquid ink. The line curls upward, breaks apart into rough scribbled fragments, then continuously reshapes into a tiny glowing jellyfish floating above the desk. The jellyfish suddenly drifts toward a nearby bookshelf. The animation moves first, then the handheld camera reacts a fraction of a second later, quickly panning and stepping after it.
3–6 seconds: The jellyfish slips between two books. Its tentacles stretch into loose scribbles, its body collapses into uneven colored strokes, and the entire drawing continuously morphs into a small orange fox made from glowing crayon lines. The fox jumps down from the shelf, runs across the floor, then dives beneath the bed. The animation escapes first while the camera hesitates, tilts downward, then follows slightly late with imperfect handheld movement.
6–10 seconds: Under the bed, the orange fox stretches unnaturally long. Its legs dissolve into restless pencil strokes while its body twists and continuously reshapes into a green lizard. As it crawls out from the opposite side, the lizard's body fragments into fluttering chalk marks and morphs into a flock of tiny purple birds. The birds spiral around the room before merging together, their rough strokes tangling and continuously transforming into a large floating dragon made entirely from hand-drawn lines. The dragon rushes toward the bedroom door first, forcing the camera operator to stand, turn, and chase after it with delayed, shaky smartphone movement.
10–13 seconds: The dragon crashes into a hanging jacket beside the door without physically damaging it. Its body scatters into hundreds of glowing sketch marks that crawl across the fabric. The jacket suddenly develops two rough cartoon arms and a smiling face. Its smile stretches wider as the colored strokes break apart, twist, overlap, and continuously morph the friendly jacket character into a strange fuzzy monster with oversized eyes and crooked teeth. The monster jumps toward the ceiling first, while the camera jerks upward a moment later and struggles briefly to regain focus.
13–15 seconds: The monster splashes across the ceiling as loose crayon strokes. The strokes spread rapidly across the surface, curl together, and continuously reshape into a gigantic hand-drawn moon face covering most of the ceiling. Its eyes open, blink once, then its mouth stretches into a playful grin. The face suddenly looks toward the bedroom door as the last glowing strokes ripple across the walls. The animation reacts first, then the camera slowly tilts and drifts after its gaze with a noticeably delayed handheld response.
All animated elements must feel physically integrated into the live-action room while remaining unmistakably handmade. Use rough crayon, chalk, colored-pencil, dry-brush, and scribbled textures, irregular outlines, visible paper-like grain within the strokes, imperfect fills, fuzzy edges, uneven opacity, and subtle frame-by-frame line wobble. Transformations must happen visibly through collapsing, stretching, fragmenting, smearing, tangling, and reshaping strokes, never by making one object disappear and replacing it with another. Maintain one continuous take inside the same room with no cuts or scene transitions. The animated creatures always initiate movement first, while the person filming reacts slightly late and follows them naturally with one-handed smartphone movement. Preserve handheld shake, low-light noise, focus breathing, imperfect autofocus, motion blur, exposure fluctuations, accidental framing, and human reaction time. Environmental audio only: quiet room tone, footsteps, fabric movement, floor creaks, distant outdoor ambience, refrigerator hum, subtle breathing, and natural handling noise from the phone. No overly precise 3D CGI, excessively smooth vector lines, neon-tube-like visuals, perfectly stabilized gimbal footage, overly cinematic lighting, polished advertising-style compositions, subtitles, logos, or background music.

【摄影规则】

【最终强制约束】

Generate a 30-second horizontal 16:9 realistic fitness lifestyle influencer vlog from the provided first frame.
Style: Realistic daily fitness influencer vlog, natural indoor lighting, casual social media filming style, warm private gym atmosphere. The video should feel like a smooth everyday workout vlog filmed by an influencer, with natural movement, clean pacing, and coherent camera transitions.
Character: One main character only: Maya, a young adult female fitness creator with brown hair in a high ponytail, wearing a taupe long-sleeve athletic top, matching leggings, white socks, and light grey training shoes. Keep her face, hairstyle, outfit, body type, and identity consistent throughout the video.
Scene: A quiet private indoor gym with dark grey walls, black rubber floor, warm ceiling lights, a workout bench, clear plastic water bottle, small towel, gym bag, small dumbbells, mirror area, chair, and wall-mounted drinking fountain. Keep the environment consistent. Objects should stay in believable positions.
Camera style: Use two smooth camera perspectives: 1. Selfie camera perspective: Maya holds the camera or phone at arm’s length, showing her face and upper body. 2. Third-person camera perspective: stable camera placed near the bench or mirror, showing her full body and workout actions.
Camera transitions: Transitions must feel smooth and intentional, like a polished influencer vlog edit. Use gentle cuts, soft handheld reframing, slow push-ins, and small pans. Each shot should last long enough to feel natural. Avoid rapid cutting, sudden jumps, extreme zooms, spinning camera, or chaotic handheld movement.
Action flow: All actions should connect naturally: Maya places her bag, adjusts her hair, introduces the workout, picks up a dumbbell, does a short set, rests, drinks water, stretches, checks the mirror, and ends with a relaxed smile. Movements should be casual, continuous, and realistic, not stiff or overposed.
Action timing: 0s - 4s: Third-person view. Maya stands beside the workout bench and calmly places her gym bag or towel on the bench. She adjusts the position of the water bottle slightly. Camera is stable, medium-wide, showing the bench and gym room.
4s - 7s: Smooth cut to selfie camera. Maya holds the camera at arm’s length, looks into the lens, gives a small natural smile, and lightly adjusts her ponytail. The camera moves gently with her hand but remains stable and readable.
7s - 10s: Selfie camera slowly tilts down and transitions to a third-person bench view. Maya lowers the camera or the edit cuts softly to the bench angle. She reaches for a small dumbbell on the floor. The movement should feel connected, not abrupt.
10s - 15s: Third-person workout shot. Maya places one hand on the bench and performs a short controlled dumbbell row set, about 3 to 4 smooth repetitions. Keep the motion steady and anatomically correct. Hair and fabric move subtly with each rep.
15s - 17s: She finishes the set, gently places the dumbbell back on the floor, and sits on the bench. Camera stays stable with a slight push-in, capturing the transition from exercise to rest.
17s - 20s: Close detail shot. Her hand reaches for the clear water bottle, opens it, and brings it up naturally. The camera follows slowly, without shaking.
20s - 22s: Selfie camera perspective. Maya takes a small drink, exhales, and looks into the lens with a relaxed expression. Her breathing feels natural after the set.
22s - 25s: Smooth cut to third-person view near the mirror. Maya stands, rolls her shoulders, stretches one arm across her chest, then switches sides. Camera gently pans to keep her centered.
25s - 27s: Handheld lifestyle detail. Maya picks up the towel, wipes her hands, and checks her ponytail in the mirror. The action is small, casual, and continuous.
27s - 30s:Final smooth ending. Maya returns beside the bench, places one hand near the water bottle, looks toward the camera, and gives a small friendly smile or nod. Camera slowly settles into a stable medium-wide frame. End on a calm natural vlog moment.
Motion quality: Realistic body mechanics, natural walking and stretching, accurate hand contact with bottle, towel, dumbbell, and bench, stable foot contact, natural breathing, subtle hair and fabric motion. No jerky actions, no sudden pose changes, no object teleporting.
Camera smoothness: Camera motion should be smooth, slow, and purposeful. Handheld shots should have only mild natural move ment. Third-person shots should feel stable. Transitions between shots should preserve continuity of position and objects.
Final output: 30 seconds, horizontal 16:9, realistic fitness influencer vlog, one female fitness creator, private indoor gym, smooth selfie and third-person camera transitions, natural daily workout flow, no subtitles, no watermark, no logo.

[0–3 seconds] Extreme close-up of the writer's face emerging from near-total black. A narrow cream-colored strip of light slides across her eyes. The frame abruptly opens sideways like torn paper, revealing her full silhouette walking across a burnt-red background while loose sheets of paper trail behind her like a long ribbon.
[3–6 seconds] The paper ribbon sweeps across frame and becomes a graphic wipe. Reveal her in profile at a desk. She strikes one typewriter key. On impact, the screen fractures into three bold rectangular panels: her gloved fingers, the metal typebar snapping forward, and a giant black ink letter striking paper.
[6–9 seconds] Rapid rhythmic close-ups: spinning typewriter ribbon spool, carriage return lever snapping sideways, black ink spreading through rough paper fibers. Thin cream lines cut diagonally across the screen and reorganize the images into an asymmetric editorial collage.
[9–12 seconds] Pull wide. The writer stands alone beside an enormous abstract typewriter rendered as a black geometric silhouette. She pulls one endless page upward. The rising page becomes a full-frame cream vertical wipe while scattered black letters tumble downward like physical debris.
[12–15 seconds] The letters rapidly assemble into the exact title "INK AFTER DARK" centered large on a burnt-red paper field. The writer's small black silhouette crosses beneath the title and exits frame. The title appears through sharp letter-by-letter mechanical impacts over 0.5 seconds, holds completely still through the ending. No bouncing, spinning, stretching, or fly-in typography.
[CAMERA]
Use aggressive graphic changes in scale: extreme facial close-up → full-body silhouette → macro mechanical inserts → monumental wide composition.
Camera movement should feel designed rather than realistic: fast lateral pushes, sudden graphic crops, one rapid pull-out, and precise locked compositions. Avoid conventional cinematic orbit shots.
[LIGHT]

Hard noir side-lighting translated into flat graphic shapes. Rough vintage print stock, subtle paper scratches, coarse ink grain, slight registration offsets, and occasional frame jitter.
[EDIT]
Fast editorial rhythm with hard cuts, paper wipes, diagonal panel slices, oversized object masks, and split-screen recompositions.
Transitions must be motivated by paper, ink, typewriter mechanisms, or moving silhouettes. No soft dissolves.
Make every shot feel newly composed rather than simply zooming into the previous image.
[AUDIO]
Audio: dry typewriter key strikes, paper slides, ribbon-spool clicks, carriage-return snaps, faint room hum, and one heavy mechanical impact when the final title locks.
BGM: an original 15-second cue, 65% noir suspense and 35% cool jazz. Upright bass, brushed snare, muted vibraphone, sparse low piano, and short clipped brass accents. Begin almost empty, introduce bass at 3 seconds, rhythmic percussion at 6 seconds, a brief brass accent at 10 seconds, then freeze the final 2 seconds on one bass note and the mechanical title hit. Do not imitate an existing melody.
[NEGATIVE]
No subtitles, extra on-screen text, watermarks, platform logos, or stickers.
Do not introduce Chinese text, garbled characters, misspellings, or additional title variations. Render "INK AFTER DARK" once only.
No 3D CGI, photorealism, anime styling, glossy modern motion graphics, neon cyberpunk aesthetics, or smooth vector-clean surfaces.

title: Twin Blades vs Halberd
prompt:

角色和方向全程锁死：绯始终在画面左侧，黑发、朱红破斗篷、双手各持一把朱砂弯短刃，左→右主动贴身压进；澜始终在右侧，靛蓝黑衣、双手持一柄黑玉长戟，右→左以长兵器控距反击。场景固定为断桥A—湿墨石桥桥面B—倒塌门楼C，远处灰墨瀑布。全程锁定横向屏轴，受控切镜；只能在真实碰撞、墨爆、碎石掠镜或人物掠镜时切镜，切后必须接住同一运动方向和余势。
0-2秒：低机位贴桥跟拍，绯从断桥A贴地疾冲，双刃一低一高拖出朱红湿墨；澜从门楼C封住中线后右→左横扫。绯双刃交叉硬架戟刃，刃戟在中央明确撞击，先压出黑白飞白小核，再出现双方短促后坐。
2-4秒：绯借反震滑步贴进戟杆内圈，完成①挑开戟杆、②左刃压肩线、③右刃横切的内线三连；澜旋身收戟连续格开，随后戟尾钉桥借力，整身右→左低位横扫。绯双刃压地后仰滑退，戟风擦裂桥石。
4-6秒：澜沿桥追压，戟杆直推胸线；绯踩断桥矮栏起跳翻越长戟。空中完成①双刃交剪压戟、②翻腕下切、③双刃合剪下劈；澜竖戟硬封，碰撞力将两人压向桥面，落点炸起纵向红蓝墨柱。
6-8秒：墨柱遮镜切换，真实反作用力把双方短暂打散：绯化作向左回射的朱红楔形长笔，澜化作向右回射的靛蓝长笔；两条笔锋到桥端后立刻折返，在桥面重新凝成人形、双刃与长戟，绝不停顿。
8-10秒：绯再次近身压制，①低刃扫腿线、②肩撞贴入、③右刃斜劈；澜连挡后用戟柄回磕绯，再以戟尾砸裂桥面。绯被震向左后方贴地滑出，碎石和蓝墨沿地面喷射。

title: The Night Was Ending But She Had
prompt:
Create a 15 second photorealistic nightlife video in native 16:9, one continuous handheld take with no cuts. Scene: an open rooftop parking deck at night, dark asphalt with parking lines, blue perimeter fencing, concrete barriers, distant modern buildings with tiny red aviation lights, occasional blurred traffic, and tall white LED parking lamps. A glossy black luxury car sits close to camera with the front passenger door open. The door frame forms a strong diagonal foreground shape from lower center toward upper left, while the black side mirror fills the lower right with cool cyan reflections.
A stylish young adult woman with warm medium skin, long straight dark hair, natural makeup, small hoop earrings, delicate bracelets, and a fitted metallic silver strapless top sits sideways in the passenger seat and leans into the doorway. Keep her face, hair, proportions, wardrobe, jewelry, car, and environment consistent. Her behavior feels spontaneous and playful, as if a friend is filming her after a night out.
Seconds 0 to 2: medium close shot from outside the passenger door at chest level, roughly 28 mm smartphone lens. She looks upward past camera, lifts one hand behind her head, and lightly brushes her hair. Camera floats gently with natural hand tremor.
Seconds 2 to 4: she turns toward camera, lowers her hand near her cheek and collarbone, smiles, and leans a little closer. Her gaze briefly follows the person filming instead of staring rigidly into the lens.
Seconds 4 to 6: she brings fingertips to her lips and blows one playful kiss, then eases backward into the seat. Her shoulders rotate naturally and her hair shifts. Camera drifts right so the open door edge partially hides her.
Seconds 6 to 9: she raises a dark smartphone to her ear, smiles as if reacting to someone, then lowers it and looks at the screen. Keep tiny natural pauses between gestures.
Seconds 9 to 12: she extends the phone outward in her right hand as if taking a selfie or recording herself, adjusts the angle with her wrist, tilts her head back, and laughs softly. Her free hand touches her hair. Camera slowly moves farther right and slightly backward, revealing more empty parking deck and blue fencing.
Seconds 12 to 15: she keeps the phone outward, leans lower into the seat, gives a final playful head tilt and relaxed smile, then settles naturally. End slightly off center with the side mirror prominent and city lights softly blurred behind her.
Use only believable practical lighting. Cool teal and neutral white parking lamp spill, warm natural skin, bright car reflections, soft facial shadows, faint hair rim light, mild highlight clipping around lamps, realistic low light sensor noise, slight motion blur, tiny exposure breathing, occasional focus hunting, visible skin texture, flyaway hairs, fabric creases, fingerprints and micro reflections. Preserve realistic anatomy and hand motion. Avoid beauty filter skin, perfect stabilization, warped fingers, floating jewelry, rubbery facial motion, excessive slow motion, fake fog, impossible reflections, or stylized effects.
Camera character: premium smartphone footage, handheld but controlled, subtle rolling shutter, real autofocus, modest depth of field, natural perspective, 24 frames per second feel, realistic shutter blur. No text, logos, subtitles, transitions, or visual effects.
Audio: nocturnal club and R and B instrumental around 150 BPM, deep rounded kick, tight percussion, soft sub bass, restrained atmospheric synths, no vocals. Keep faint parking deck ambience underneath with distant traffic and open air city noise. Let beat accents loosely match the hair touch, blown kiss, phone raise, and final head tilt.

title: Bollywood Action Behind The Scenes
prompt:

The sequence takes place on a controlled multi-lane highway set in daytime. Several large matte-black armored SUVs and tactical vehicles are driving fast in the same direction, tightly coordinated like a convoy. A male Bollywood stunt performer in black tactical clothing and protective gear is already running on top of one armored vehicle while the whole convoy is moving.
The phone camera struggles to keep him centered as he sprints across the roof. Fake gunfire erupts from another vehicle — practical blank-fire effects, flashes, sparks hitting the metal around him, and controlled squibs bursting nearby. He ducks instinctively, keeps running, then leaps from the roof of one moving armored car onto the next vehicle, landing hard on one knee and immediately continuing forward.
A professional camera crane / tracking arm mounted to another pursuit vehicle is visible moving alongside the convoy, carrying a cinema camera that follows the stuntman without blocking him. The stuntman jumps again onto another armored vehicle, nearly slips from the roof because of the speed, grabs a roof rail, swings himself back up, and keeps running while more fake bullets spark around him. The convoy swerves slightly in formation, making the stunt feel even more dangerous.

Audio: raw mobile-phone production sound only — wind distortion, engines, tire noise, fake gunfire, metal impacts, crew shouting, radio chatter, stuntman breathing, and finally the loud “CUT!” call.

title: The Dog Dropping The Ball Halfway Is
prompt:
CAMERA: Handheld DV 16mm daily vlog footage. The video MUST begin with her holding the camera at arm's length in selfie mode while stepping outside her apartment building with her dog. The first 20–30 seconds are entirely handheld. Later she occasionally places the camera on a park bench, low stone wall, picnic table, or the ground for wider shots. Keep subtle handheld shake, drifting composition, autofocus hunting, rushed reframing, uneven zooms, exposure breathing, brief accidental face cropping, and imperfect framing throughout. The camera itself is never visible.
LOOK: Warm analog tape texture with gentle film grain, slightly softened sharpness, subtle halation around sunlight, realistic skin tones, low contrast, tiny exposure shifts, and natural motion blur. Authentic footage from someone's everyday life rather than a polished commercial.
STYLE: A relaxed morning lifestyle vlog. Quiet, cozy, spontaneous. She occasionally laughs at her dog, pauses to look around, adjusts the leash, brushes hair away from her face, and speaks naturally in short sentences with comfortable pauses.
CHARACTER: EMMA, mid-20s. Long light brown hair in a messy ponytail, green eyes, minimal makeup, oversized gray hoodie, black biker shorts, white sneakers, small crossbody bag. Walking a happy golden retriever.
SETTING: A peaceful suburban neighborhood on a sunny morning. Tree-lined sidewalks, quiet residential streets, birds singing, a small park with benches, green grass, soft golden morning light. Very few people around.
SCENES: Opens in selfie mode, leaving the apartment building, dog pulling excitedly on the leash. "Good morning." Smiles. "Someone couldn't wait." The dog sniffs everything as they walk. Quiet laugh. "He has to inspect every single tree." Still handheld, into a small park. The dog stops and stares at a squirrel. "Oh... there we go." Small headshake. She sets the camera on a bench for a wider angle and throws a tennis ball. The dog chases it. "Worth waking up early." Picks the camera back up, walking slowly, looks up at the trees. "It's actually really peaceful out here." The dog returns with the ball but drops it halfway. She laughs. "Close enough." She sits on the bench, dog lying beside her, scratching behind his ears. "I think he's happier than I am." Stands, keeps walking, selfie mode heading home. "Coffee is definitely next." Smiles into the lens. "See you later." Small wave, ends the recording.
A few things worth noticing about why it's built this way:
The dog is the unpredictability engine. Stopping at a squirrel, dropping the ball halfway, inspecting every tree. An animal doing animal things gives the scene a randomness that a scripted human beat never would.
The camera gets put down and picked back up. Handheld, then propped on a bench for the wide, then handheld again. That rhythm is what an actual vlogger does, and it's why the wide shots don't feel like a different production.
Every line is four words or fewer. "Close enough." "Worth waking up early." Nobody narrates in full sentences while walking a dog.
And the camera block is a list of mistakes on purpose. Autofocus hunting, accidental face cropping, drifting composition. Every one is a flaw, and every one is doing the heavy lifting.

Create a 30-second, 16:9 ultra-realistic handheld lifestyle vlog following the same young Korean woman from the reference image through an ordinary day in Seoul. Keep her face, identity, hairstyle, body, outfit, accessories, and proportions perfectly consistent.
She wears a light-blue oversized shirt over a white fitted T-shirt, dark-gray straight jeans, white sneakers, brown crossbody bag, and silver watch throughout.
Style: Genuine footage filmed casually by a close friend on a smartphone/compact camera. Handheld shake, imperfect framing, autofocus/exposure shifts, natural motion blur, mild digital noise, realistic skin texture, occasional late camera reactions. No gimbal, drone, cinematic choreography, slow motion, beauty filter, or commercial look.
0–5s: Quiet Seoul neighborhood. She leaves her apartment, checks her phone, notices the camera, smiles sleepily, fixes her hair and says naturally: “오늘도 같이 가자.”
5–11s: Enters a tiny neighborhood bakery, notices a fresh pastry and says: “이거 냄새 너무 좋다.” Buys it, takes a bite outside, and smiles at the camera.
11–17s: Boards a local bus and sits by the window. Seoul streets pass outside with realistic reflections and sunlight. She quietly says: “이런 날은 그냥 걷고 싶어.”
17–23s: Gets off near a riverside path. Buys a fruit cup from a small cart. A bicycle passes unexpectedly close; she steps aside, laughs, and says: “방금 좀 놀랐어.”
23–27s: Golden-hour riverside. She sits on a bench, places the fruit cup beside her, removes one earbud, watches the water, and gives a small genuine smile as the wind moves her hair.
27–30s: She stands and walks away. After a few steps, looks back and says: “다음엔 너도 같이 와.” She continues walking as the camera follows behind. Recording naturally ends around 29.5s.
REALISM: Accurate human biomechanics, grounded feet, continuous objects, realistic bus movement, natural walking/eating/sitting, consistent architecture and wardrobe. No teleportation, morphing, identity drift, duplicated/disappearing objects, distorted hands or limbs.
AUDIO: Natural Korean dialogue with accurate lip-sync, phone-mic quality, footsteps, traffic, birds, bakery sounds, bus engine, bicycle, wind and city ambience. No music, narrator, or cinematic SFX.
Absolutely no subtitles, captions, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, or UI.

title: Martial Arts Lesson Teacher Her Pupils
prompt:
Young Chinese woman in her mid-20s, naturally beautiful, realistic skin texture, minimal natural makeup, calm disciplined confident personality. Long black hair tied into a neat high bun with a few loose strands, sharp focused eyes. Wearing a traditional fitted red and black martial arts uniform with a black sash, cloth training shoes. Maintain the same face, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions and overall appearance throughout.
Group of young pupils, ages 8 to 12, mixed boys and girls, wearing plain white training uniforms with colored sashes, hair neatly tied back. Maintain consistent appearance throughout.
LOCATION
A traditional martial arts courtyard at a quiet training school in the early morning. Wooden training dummies along one side, stone flooring, red pillars, a large open courtyard with soft morning mist, tall trees swaying gently beyond low walls, sunlight beginning to filter through.
CAMERA / VISUAL STYLE
Cinematic handheld footage with smooth deliberate movement, as if filmed by a respectful onlooker. Crisp natural lighting, soft morning haze, shallow depth of field on close-up techniques, wider steady shots capturing group formations, subtle warm color grading, gentle motion blur on fast movements.
No shaky chaotic camera work, no overly stylized slow-motion excess — kept authentic and respectful.
— MORNING GATHERING
The pupils stand in neat rows across the courtyard, quiet and attentive, as the woman walks out to face them, hands clasped behind her back.
She bows respectfully toward the group. The pupils bow back in unison.
— BEGINNING THE LESSON
She says calmly, "Today we focus on balance before power."
She demonstrates a slow, controlled stance, shifting her weight smoothly between her legs.
The pupils watch closely, some mimicking the movement slightly out of sync.
— CORRECTING A PUPIL
She walks along the rows, pausing beside a young boy struggling with his stance.
She gently adjusts his shoulders and feet, saying, "Root yourself like a tree. Strong, but flexible."
The boy nods, adjusting his posture, and she gives an encouraging nod back.
— DEMONSTRATING A TECHNIQUE
She steps to the front and performs a fluid combination of strikes and blocks, precise and controlled, her uniform sleeves snapping crisply with each movement.
The pupils watch in quiet awe, a few whispering excitedly to each other.
— PRACTICE TOGETHER
She calls out, "Now, together — slowly."
The pupils mirror her movements as a group, counting softly under their breath, her voice guiding their rhythm.
She moves through the rows, offering small corrections and quiet words of encouragement.
— A MOMENT OF ENCOURAGEMENT
One young girl completes the sequence correctly and looks up hopefully.
The woman smiles warmly and says, "Very good. You are learning patience, not just movement."
The girl beams with pride, standing a little taller.
— FINAL MOMENT
The lesson winds down as morning light fully fills the courtyard.
The pupils line up again, bowing together as she bows back with quiet pride.
She says softly, "Discipline today becomes strength tomorrow. Same time, same place."
The pupils disperse gradually, chatting excitedly, as she remains standing calmly in the courtyard, the camera lingering on her still, composed presence.
AUDIO: Soft morning birdsong, rustling leaves, the woman's calm instructive voice, pupils' footsteps and light chatter, fabric movement during techniques, distant temple bells. No music, no added narration, no subtitles.
FINAL FEEL: A calm, respectful portrayal of discipline and mentorship — grounded, authentic, quietly inspiring. Real teaching dynamics, genuine effort from young pupils, cinematic but humble presentation. No exaggerated action-movie flair — just real skill, patience, and connection between teacher and students.

title: Hidden Blind Box Unboxing Reveal
prompt:
Duration: 30秒
Aspect ratio: 9:16
Language: 中文普通话
人物参考: @​ 
Audio: 女主现场对白、同一女声画外旁白、电子潮流音乐、拆盒声、机关声、变身音效；无字幕
Overall style: 写实开箱Vlog结合潮流奇幻广告，真实手机摄影，后半段转为高质感时尚棚拍
GLOBAL CONTINUITY
女主：
全程只有 图片1一名成年女主，保持五官、体型和声音一致。开场发型、穿着沿用参考图；完成变身后才更换隐藏款造型。
原创盲盒主题：
“星云双生隐藏款”。与原片朋克盲盒完全不同。
包装设计：
黑银色六边形陨石舱，表面覆盖蓝紫极光纹理；正面是半透明星形观察窗，顶部有可旋转的月牙锁扣，侧面带全息拉环。包装只使用星月图标，不出现可读品牌文字。
公仔设计：
公仔五官明显参考 图片1，头身比约1:2.5，精致潮玩质感。头发沿头部中线对半分染：画面左侧电光蓝，画面右侧星云紫，整齐刘海，两束渐变长发。穿银紫色不对称星云短裙、半透明肩部装饰、月牙腰带、蓝紫渐变厚底短靴，脚下是发光星形底座。
真人隐藏款造型：
真人变身后完整还原公仔设计：半蓝半紫头发、星云妆容、银紫未来感服装和透明配饰，但仍保持真实人类比例与 图片1身份。
DRAMATIC ENGINE
钩子：开出一个长得和自己一模一样的隐藏款。
升级：公仔突然启动，女主变成它的真人版本。
展示：真人与公仔同步动作，证明两者存在神秘连接。
反转：包装说明“隐藏款只能存在一个”，女主最终变成第二只公仔。
SHOT 1（00:00-00:05.00）打开陨石舱
Environment:
舒适现代卧室，桌面整洁，背景带少量蓝紫氛围灯。
Action:
女主将六边形盲盒放到桌上，先撕开星形封条，再旋转月牙锁扣。盒体像花瓣一样向六个方向展开，内部升起带星形底座的公仔。蓝紫微光映在她脸上。
Camera:
第一人称开箱式近景开始，随后切至女主与盒子同框的中景；手部和开盒步骤必须清楚。
旁白（00:00.40-00:03.80）：
“今天开一个，据说只有百分之一概率出现的星云隐藏款。”
Voice:
自然Vlog语气，略带期待；“百分之一”轻微加重。
Performance:
女主开始专注拆盒；看见公仔脸部后动作突然停住，眉毛抬起，眼睛稍微睁大，但不夸张尖叫。
SHOT 2（00:05.00-00:10.00）发现公仔就是自己
Action:
女主双手托起公仔，先看公仔，再快速看向镜头；将公仔转到侧面，展示一半蓝色、一半紫色的头发和星云服装。随后把公仔靠近自己的脸进行对比。
Dialogue（00:06.00-00:08.60）：
“等一下……它怎么长得这么像我？”
Voice:
“等一下”轻声迟疑；停顿0.3秒；后半句加快，带真实惊讶。
Face:
视线在公仔与镜头之间来回两次，嘴唇微张，最后露出难以置信的浅笑。
Camera:
公仔超近景、头发侧面特写、女主与公仔同框近景。不得让公仔五官变成其他人物。
SHOT 3（00:10.00-00:14.00）机关启动
Action:
公仔胸前的星形宝石自动亮起，头部缓慢转向女主，并眨眼一次。女主伸出食指轻碰星形宝石；一道蓝紫光环从公仔向外扩散，扫过镜头和女主全身。
Dialogue（00:10.50-00:11.70）：
“它在发光？”
Voice:
音量放轻，尾音上扬；说完立即屏住呼吸。
Transformation:
光环经过头部时，女主头发变成左侧电光蓝、右侧星云紫；光环向下扫过身体时，服装逐层变成真人隐藏款造型。变身连续、干净，没有身体扭曲。
Camera:
从公仔胸前宝石快速拉至女主面部，再沿身体向下扫描；蓝紫光环作为遮挡完成服装替换。
SHOT 4（00:14.00-00:22.00）真人隐藏款展示
Environment:
四个原创纯色棚拍空间依次切换：冰蓝、深紫、镜面银、星空黑。没有文字背景。
旁白（00:14.20-00:18.30）：
“隐藏机关启动后，开盒的人会变成它的真人版本。”
Voice:
带一点神秘广告感，清楚平稳，不盖过音乐。
Action:
00:14.00-00:16.00：冰蓝背景，女主转身展示半蓝半紫头发，两束头发随动作甩开。
00:16.00-00:18.00：深紫背景，怼脸特写；她轻抬下巴，用手指划过眼侧星云妆。
00:18.00-00:20.00：镜面银背景，低角度全身镜头；她向前一步，厚底短靴落地卡点。
00:20.00-00:22.00：星空黑背景，她完成半圈旋转，停在与公仔包装图一致的招牌姿势。
Performance:
表情由惊讶转为自信、俏皮。动作像潮流玩具广告，干净有力，不跳完整舞蹈。
Transitions:
每次以头发甩动、手掌遮镜、靴子落地完成硬切。禁止复制原片的英文大字背景。
SHOT 5（00:22.00-00:25.50）动作同步
Environment:
回到卧室桌前。女主保持真人隐藏款造型，公仔站在发光底座上。
Action:
女主歪头，公仔同步歪头；女主抬起右手，公仔延迟0.2秒做出同样动作。女主立刻收回手，惊讶地看着公仔。
Dialogue（00:23.00-00:25.00）：
“连动作都一模一样？”
Voice:
前半句压低，最后“ 一样”明显上扬。
Face:
她先觉得有趣地笑一下；发现公仔真的同步后，笑容逐渐消失，眉心轻收。
SHOT 6（00:25.50-00:30.00）隐藏款反转
旁白（00:25.50-00:27.40）：
“可盒底还写着：隐藏款只能有一个。”
Voice:
语速放慢，“只能有一个”降低音调，制造悬念。
Action:
公仔突然独立眨眼，星形底座发出蓝紫脉冲。女主低头看见自己的手指开始呈现光滑潮玩材质，惊讶抬眼。
Dialogue（00:27.60-00:29.00）：
“等等……我才是盲盒？”
Voice:
先短促吸气；“我才是”加重；结尾带困惑和慌张，但不尖叫。
Ending:
蓝紫光环横向扫过画面，利用光幕匹配剪辑：全尺寸女主消失，桌面出现第二只与她完全相同的18厘米公仔。两只公仔并排站在星形底座上，一只蓝光、一只紫光。镜头缓慢拉远，露出空椅子和已经打开的六边形包装，最后两只公仔同时眨眼，定格。
PERFORMANCE CONSTRAINTS
- 旁白为画外音，旁白期间女主嘴巴不跟读。
- 现场对白必须使用准确中文口型。
- 女主、公仔、真人变身造型必须保持同一张脸的识别特征。
- 头发严格沿中线分为蓝色与紫色，左右颜色全程不交换。
- 开盒必须表现“撕封条—旋转锁扣—盒体展开—公仔升起”。
- 真人变公仔使用蓝紫光幕匹配剪辑，不表现痛苦或身体挤压。
- 无字幕、无背景文字、无品牌标志。
NEGATIVE
旁白时人物跟着张嘴，错误说话者，lip-sync drift，robotic delivery，
盲盒变成普通纸袋，复制原片粉黑朋克公仔，英文大字背景，
头发颜色交换，蓝紫颜色混成单色，公仔脸变成陌生人，
公仔尺寸不断变化，公仔突然复制过多，额外人物，
恐怖变身，身体压缩过程，身体融化，断肢，疼痛表情，
warped faces, melting features, extra limbs, fused fingers,
identity drift, wardrobe drift, plastic human skin before final transformation,
camera jumps, abrupt room changes, unreadable package text,
subtitles, Chinese text, English text, watermarks, logos

title: Shes Spending Evening Her Favorite
prompt:
Create a 30-second 16:9 ultra-realistic casual smartphone lifestyle vlog featuring one young Korean woman going out to meet her friends, spending a fun time together, and then returning home.
The entire video must look like genuine personal footage casually recorded on a real handheld smartphone. Mostly she films herself in selfie mode, with a few natural clips filmed by one of her friends. Use imperfect framing, subtle hand shake, realistic smartphone autofocus, automatic exposure changes, slight motion blur, walking jolts, natural background sounds and authentic real-world physics. No cinematic shots, no drone, no gimbal, no beauty filters, no commercial look.
Character: The same Korean woman throughout the entire video, petite oval face, brown eyes, natural coral lips, realistic fair skin and long black hair. Maintain perfect character consistency with no face morphing, identity drift or duplicate people. She speaks naturally in Korean with accurate lip synchronization.
STORY — A DAY OUT WITH FRIENDS
0:00–0:04 — Leaving Home
She stands outside her home holding her phone in selfie mode, looking excited and ready to go out. She says naturally in Korean:
“오늘 친구들이랑 만나러 가요!”
She smiles, starts walking, and the phone shakes slightly with her steps.
0:04–0:08 — Meeting Her Friends
She arrives at a lively meeting spot and spots her friends waiting for her. Still holding her phone, she excitedly walks toward them. They naturally greet each other, smile, wave and share a quick friendly hug.
She laughs and says:
“드디어 만났다!”
0:08–0:12 — Walking Together
One of her friends casually films with a smartphone while the group walks together, laughing and talking naturally. The footage feels spontaneous, slightly imperfect and genuinely recorded by a friend.
0:12–0:16 — Food and Fun
They sit together at a casual café or restaurant. She records short clips of the food, then turns the phone toward herself and her friends while they laugh together and enjoy their meal.
0:16–0:20 — Fun Activity Together
The friends do a simple fun activity together, such as visiting an arcade, taking funny photo booth pictures, or playing a casual game. They laugh naturally and react spontaneously.
0:20–0:24 — Happy Group Moment
She records herself with all her friends gathered around. Everyone waves or makes playful expressions toward the phone camera. Keep the interaction natural and not posed like a professional photoshoot.
0:24–0:27 — Saying Goodbye
The friends say goodbye outside. They wave and casually hug before going in different directions. She watches them leave and smiles warmly.
0:27–0:30 — Back Home
Hard cut to her arriving back home. In selfie mode, looking happily tired after the day, she says:
“오늘 진짜 너무 재밌었어요. 이제 집에 왔어요!”
She smiles, waves at the camera and says:
“안녕!”
She naturally lowers the phone to end the vlog.
CRITICAL REALISM REQUIREMENTS: Prioritize genuine smartphone vlog footage: arm-length selfie framing, natural switches between front and rear cameras, occasional imperfect composition, autofocus delays, exposure fluctuations, subtle hand shake, realistic walking movement, spontaneous laughter, natural blinking and breathing, authentic conversations and background activity. Friends should behave naturally like real friends, not actors posing for a commercial. The final result must look like a genuine personal day-out vlog recorded casually on a smartphone.

title: What Could You Create You Had
prompt:
30 seconds | 16:9 | Ultra-photorealistic live-action
Create a natural Korean summer day-in-the-life video featuring one young Korean man spending a quiet afternoon preparing a simple chilled fruit snack at home.
Use the reference image only for his exact facial identity, hairstyle, skin tone, and body proportions. Keep his appearance consistent throughout the entire video.
OUTFIT: Lightweight pale-yellow short-sleeve shirt, loose white cotton pants, simple canvas shoulder bag, clean white low-profile sneakers, minimal silver watch. Outfit remains unchanged from beginning to end.
TIME & LIGHTING: Warm late-afternoon summer sunlight. Consistent weather, shadows, color temperature, and time of day across every scene.
00–05s — Neighborhood walk
He leaves a small Korean apartment building carrying his canvas shoulder bag and walks down a quiet residential street.
Trees move gently in the summer breeze. Parked scooters, apartment entrances, utility poles, bicycles, parked cars, and distant pedestrians create an authentic Korean neighborhood atmosphere.
The camera naturally follows him as he walks.
He briefly looks toward the camera and casually says:
“I need something refreshing today.”
His expression is relaxed and natural, not posed.
05–10s — Local fruit stand
He arrives at a small neighborhood fruit shop with crates of peaches, grapes, melons, Korean pears, and other seasonal fruit.
Instead of immediately choosing something, he slowly walks around comparing the fruit.
He notices a basket of ripe peaches, picks one up carefully, examines its surface, smells it, and gives a subtle satisfied smile.
The shop owner casually says something off-camera.
He responds naturally:
“This one looks perfect.”
He places several peaches into his canvas shoulder bag.
10–15s — Walking home
He walks back through the neighborhood carrying the slightly heavier bag.
The camera follows naturally from behind and then moves alongside him.
He adjusts the shoulder bag against his body as the peaches shift naturally inside.
A bicycle passes in the background.
Leaves move gently in the breeze. His hair moves subtly with the air.
His walking pace and body movements remain completely natural and unscripted.
15–21s — Apartment kitchen
He enters his apartment kitchen and places the peaches carefully on the counter.

Early Kodachrome, warm saturation in reds and yellows, weak blues, green cast in shadow. Gate weave, frame breathing side to side. Dust and hair on the gate, one vertical scratch, one splice jump. Halation glow on highlights. Heavy grain. Undercranked 16 frames per second played at 24 so movement is slightly too fast and jerky. Rounded soft corners, mild vignette. No digital sharpness.
BEATS
0:00 to 0:04 Frame is tilted and pointed at the ground, then swings up through blown out sky. Her voice arrives before her face does.
0:04 to 0:08 He finds her, far too close, cropping her forehead. She steps back and mimes holding the camera lower with both hands. He does not adjust.
0:08 to 0:12 Dead air. He simply holds on her, too long, saying nothing. She runs out of things to instruct, drops her hands, and just stands there smiling at her father rather than at a lens. Wind moves the leaves.

Diegetic only. Nothing dramatic happens on purpose. No posing, no waving for the camera, no sentimental staging, no hero framing, no golden hour beauty lighting. The love is entirely in how badly it is shot and how long he keeps it on her. If she performs for the lens the illusion breaks.

LAST FRAME
Tilted frame of bare flagstones and the edge of a sandal, badly exposed, weaving, image fading as the spring winds down, then hard cut to black. Absolutely no on screen text, no title card, no lettering, no numbers, no logo, no signage of any kind in the final frame.

title: This Looks Like A Travel Vlog Thats
prompt:
CAMERA: Single unbroken handheld boyfriend vlog take throughout, 30 seconds total. The camera feels like a real boyfriend holding a small mirrorless camera or phone, not a professional production. Natural handheld movement, imperfect framing, occasional camera shake, spontaneous reactions. Realistic autofocus adjustments, slight motion blur and natural exposure changes.
CHARACTER: Use the woman from the reference image as the main character. Maintain her exact facial identity, hairstyle, facial features, body proportions and overall appearance throughout the entire video. She must remain the same person in every shot.
Most importantly, she doesn't perform for the camera.
She sometimes notices it.
Sometimes forgets it's there.
Sometimes looks back.
Sometimes just keeps walking.
That's what makes the footage feel personal.
STORY:
0–5s - Morning at a small Tokyo apartment.
The boyfriend casually walks into the room while she fixes her hair and gets ready for the day. She notices the camera, smiles, laughs and playfully tells him to stop filming.
Nothing important happens.
That's intentional.
5–10s - Walking through Tokyo.
She leaves the apartment and walks through a quiet neighborhood. Shops are opening, bicycles pass, locals go about their morning.
She stops at a convenience store and asks the person behind the camera which drink or snack she should get.
10–18s - Local food.
They walk through a small alley into a cozy restaurant. She orders ramen, picks up the chopsticks and takes a bite.
The food is hotter than expected.
She reacts naturally and laughs while the boyfriend laughs behind the camera.
18–25s - Afternoon.
They explore a lively neighborhood. She looks through small shops, takes photos and occasionally turns back toward the camera.
The camera isn't always focused on her face.
Sometimes it's her hands.
Sometimes the street.
Sometimes the people passing by.
25–30s - Night.
Tokyo lights come on.
She walks slightly ahead, turns back and smiles.
They get on a train. She sits beside the window watching the city lights pass outside.
The camera slowly moves closer.
Cut.
WHY THIS WORKS
The prompt doesn't tell the model to create beautiful cinematic shots.
It tells the model to behave like someone who happens to be filming his girlfriend.
That's a completely different instruction.
The imperfect framing matters.
A professional camera operator would constantly correct the composition. A boyfriend wouldn't.
The pauses matter too.
Real people don't react perfectly on cue. They hesitate, look away, laugh at the wrong moment and sometimes forget they're being filmed.
And the camera shouldn't feel invisible.
Small shakes.
Autofocus hunting.
Exposure adjustments.
Slight motion blur.
Those imperfections are what sell the realism.
The biggest instruction might actually be:
She does not pose for the camera
Because the moment the subject starts performing, the footage stops feeling like a memory and starts feeling like an advertisement.
AI video is very good at making things look cinematic.
The harder test is making 30 seconds of completely ordinary life feel like someone actually lived it.

→

坠水：彻底失败

title: Japanese Water Obstacle Variety Special
prompt:
[Style] Large-scale Japanese variety show water obstacle challenge special program (Japanese TV Game Show, Live-Action Broadcast), multi-camera real-time broadcast, 4K photorealistic photography, high-saturation summer colors, real-time throughout without slow motion.
[Duration] 30 seconds
[Reference] @ Image1 defines the challenger's face, hairstyle, body proportions, and full outfit. Use only the person. Do not use the grey studio background, the reference-sheet grid layout, or the multiple-view composition. Only one HANEUL exists in the video at all times.
[Character] HANEUL — adult Korean female, early 20s, strong and healthy athletic build. Straight black chin-length bob with full blunt bangs, brown eyes, small stud earrings. Outfit exactly as @ Image1: fitted black short-sleeve crop tee, grey pinstripe pleated micro skirt with a plain white elastic waistband (no legible text), white ankle socks, black chunky platform derby shoes. She speaks only Korean.
[Scene] Sunny outdoor large leisure pool obstacle course, five stages lined up from left to right. Stage 1: 5-meter high wooden jumping platform, Tarzan rope with pulley on overhead cable. Stage 2: 3-meter diameter red and yellow circular floating disc on the water, rotating continuously at a constant speed on an underwater axis, slippery surface. Stage 3: Four square floating blocks of varying distances, bobbing up and down with the waves. Stage 4: A slanted blue slippery climbing wall with grab ropes hanging from the top. Stage 5: A huge yellow cylindrical pipe spanning the water, wet reflective vinyl surface printed with red flame patterns, rotating continuously at a constant speed by a motor, just thick enough to be hugged by arms and legs, the right end connected to a small finish platform, directly below is a clear pool with no safety mats. Background includes palm trees, large water slides, light stands, commentary booth, temporary stands full of spectators. The entire film moves from left to right.
[Screen Graphics]
Top-left corner: a fictional program emblem — a hexagonal blue-and-red shield with a stylized white water-splash silhouette and the invented wordmark "SPLASH ATTACK". Fixed position and size, semi-transparent, present in every shot. Not based on any real brand or broadcaster.
Top-right corner: a digital countdown timer in a rounded white box, large bold numerals with one decimal place. It reads 90.0 when the start buzzer sounds and counts down continuously and visibly in 0.1 steps (90.0 → 89.9 → 89.8 ...) for the entire run. It never counts up and never resets. It freezes at 63.0 the instant she falls into the water and stays frozen and dimmed for the final shot.
Opening telop (visible 00:00-00:03 only, lower third): a pink-and-white broadcast nameplate — a magenta circle on the left containing the number "07"; to its right the name "HANEUL" in large bold letters with small katakana furigana "ハヌル" printed above it; directly below, a red banner strip reading "アイドル練習生". The nameplate slides in from the left, holds, then slides out. No other on-screen text anywhere in the video.
[Fixed Items] The position, size, color, and connection of the five stages remain unchanged throughout the film; only one challenger is always in the frame; hair and clothes are dry at the start and only naturally soaked after falling into the water; the circular floating disc and yellow pipe must be continuously rotating in all shots where they appear; the corner emblem and the countdown timer stay in the same corners at the same size in every shot.
[00:00-00:03] Shot 1: Tarzan rope launch (Eye-level Medium → Wide Pull-back, ENG Camera)
Visual: She stands on the edge of the 5-meter platform holding the rope, toes gripping the edge. Opening nameplate telop on screen. Timer reads 90.0 and starts running down on the buzzer, reaching 87.0.
Dialogue (Korean): {무조건 클리어합니다!}
Action: When the buzzer sounds, she kicks off forcefully, the pulley slides right along the cable, her body swings over the water in a pendulum arc, black bob and bangs blown back by the wind.
Commentary (Japanese): {まずはターザンロープ!}
SFX: Start buzzer, pulley sliding, crowd cheering.
[00:03-00:07] Shot 2: Landing on rotating disc (Fixed Side Shot)
Visual: Fixed camera on the side of the floating disc, showing the person, rope, and disc. Timer runs from 87.0 down to 83.0.
Scene: The red and yellow circular floating disc is rotating continuously at a constant speed on the water, the slippery surface reflecting light.
Action: She releases the rope and lands on the disc; as soon as her platform soles touch, she is carried sideways and backwards by the rotation. She spreads her arms and takes small, rapid steps in the opposite direction to offset the rotation, knees bent and center of gravity low, stabilizing after a few wobbles.
Expression: Eyebrows fly up, teeth clenched, then a quick grin.
Commentary (Japanese): {回転板だ! 耐えた!}
SFX: Low-frequency hum of the turntable axis, sound of soles rubbing, a burst of cheers.
[00:07-00:12] Shot 3: Floating board jumps (Dolly Track L→R)
Camera: Dolly camera moving parallel to the direction of progress, tracking from left to right. Timer runs from 83.0 down to 78.0.
Visual: Four square floating blocks bobbing up and down with the waves, unevenly spaced.
Action: She jumps from the edge of the turntable, crossing the floating blocks with four consecutive single-foot jumps. On the second block she missteps, the block sinks sharply, her upper body lunges forward and arms circle wildly for balance. Her right foot splashes in the water before she manages to step onto the third block, and the final jump lands both feet on the fourth block.
Dialogue (Korean): {아, 위험해...!}
Commentary (Japanese): {二枚目で崩れた! でも繋いだ!}
SFX: Muffled sound of blocks hitting water, splashing, intermittent gasps from the audience.
[00:12-00:17] Shot 4: Slippery climbing wall (Front 3/4 Medium Shot)

Expression: Neck muscles tensed, forehead creased, wet bangs stuck to her forehead, breathing heavily.
Dialogue (Korean): {영차, 영차...!}
Commentary (Japanese): {滑る壁! 腕だけで登った!}
SFX: Friction on the wet wall, rope tightening, applause from the crowd.
[00:17-00:21] Shot 5: Hugging the rotating log (Rear Side Fixed Shot)
Visual: Slightly rear fixed side shot, clearly showing the pipe is rotating. Timer runs from 73.0 down to 69.0.
Scene: The yellow cylindrical pipe rotates continuously by a motor, a layer of water on the wet vinyl surface, red flame patterns rolling across the screen as it turns.
Action: She jumps from the top of the slope and straddles the base of the pipe, clamping it with her chest, stomach, arms, and legs. The rotation immediately carries her to the right; she adjusts her center of gravity in the opposite direction and shuffles toward the finish by moving her arms and legs in small increments.
Dialogue (Korean): {어, 돌아간다!?}
Commentary (Japanese): {回転丸太だ! これが最難関!}
SFX: Low-frequency motor sound, wet vinyl friction.
[00:21-00:26] Shot 6: Flipped over - Limit before finish (Front Close-up → Medium Pull-back)

Her right leg detaches first, flailing in the air, then her right hand releases to reach for the finish platform, her full weight hanging by her left arm and leg as the pipe continues to rotate right.
Expression: Veins bulging at temples, arm muscles shaking, eyes wide.
Dialogue (Korean): {안 돼, 잠깐...!}
Commentary (Japanese): {回転に負けた! あと少し!}
Connection: Right fingertips are about 20cm from the finish platform, left hand still clinging to the rotating pipe.
[00:26-00:28] Shot 7: Falling into water before finish (Fixed Side Shot)
Visual: Fixed side shot of the pipe, showing the pipe, outstretched right hand, finish platform, and the water surface directly below. Timer runs down from 64.0.
Action: As the pipe rotates further, the supporting left hand is turned to the underside and slips. Her body falls sideways into the pool under gravity, creating a large splash. The pipe continues to rotate in place after she falls. At the moment of the splash the countdown timer stops dead at 63.0 and dims, holding that value.
Dialogue (Korean): {아아악!}
Commentary (Japanese): {落ちた! 丸太に回された—!}
SFX: Loud splash, gasps from the audience.
[00:28-00:30] Shot 8: Water surface reaction ending (Water-level Close-up, Static)
Visual: Water-level front close-up, static camera, focusing on the face. The frozen dimmed timer still reads 63.0 in the top-right corner, the emblem in the top-left.
Action: She emerges from the water, wet black bob sticking to her cheeks, wipes her face, looks toward the finish with a frown, and splashes the water with her hands.
Dialogue (Korean): {아, 분해!}
Action: Turns her gaze back to the camera, frown relaxes into a shy smile, shoulders shrugging slightly. In the background, the yellow pipe is still slowly rotating.
SFX: Huge cheers and applause peaking.
[Audio] High-paced game show style BGM. Synchronized sound effects: crowd cheering, applause, laughter, start buzzer, pulley, rotating motor, splashes, friction, water drops. The challenger speaks only clear natural Korean with accurate lipsync; the commentator speaks only Japanese and is never seen on camera. No other voices. BGM lowers during dialogue.
[Camera and Editing] Natural multi-camera TV broadcast, hard cuts only. Mix of ENG, wire, dolly, water-level, and telephoto shots. Maintain 180-degree rule and left-to-right progression. No high-speed camera moves, spinning, crash zooms, or drones. No slow motion, replays, freezes, or time jumps.
[Prohibitions] Maintain consistency of face, hair, body, clothing, skin color, and number of limbs, matching @ Image1 throughout. Physics must be realistic (gravity, inertia, slipping, rotation). No teleporting, backwards movement, static air, body deformation, or background replacement. Healthy athletic variety show style; the skirt hem behaves naturally and never exposes anything, no clothing malfunctions. No real brand names, logos, watermarks, broadcaster identities, or gibberish text; the only on-screen graphics are the fictional emblem, the countdown timer, and the opening nameplate.

title: Bakery Stop Then Walk Toward The Sea
prompt:
0–3 seconds
The recording begins while the group is already walking along a narrow seaside street.
The main woman is carrying a small tote bag and talking to a friend beside her.
She suddenly notices a tiny local bakery and stops mid-sentence to point at it.
The friend filming keeps walking for a moment before realizing she has stopped, creating a natural moment of camera movement and reframing.
A scooter passes behind them and briefly enters the frame.
3–6 seconds
They step inside the small bakery.
The camera remains handheld and casually follows them from behind.
The main woman looks through the display, picks something unexpectedly large, and laughs when her friend reacts to it.
She turns toward the camera while still laughing, but the camera is slightly off-center and briefly crops part of her face.
Natural indoor-to-outdoor exposure adjustment when they leave.
6–9 seconds
Outside again, the group walks toward a quieter road overlooking the sea.
The main woman opens the bakery bag while walking and offers a bite to one of her friends.
The friend refuses jokingly, making everyone laugh.
A sudden breeze moves her hair and clothing.
The camera operator tries to keep up, briefly pointing toward the ground before recovering the framing.
9–12 seconds
They reach a small overlook above the water.
Instead of posing, everyone casually leans against the railing and looks toward the ocean.
The main woman notices a boat in the distance and tries to point it out while talking.
Another friend steps directly in front of the phone while joking around, partially blocking the view for a moment.
The camera operator laughs and shifts sideways to see around them.
12–15 seconds
The group begins heading down a narrow path toward the beach.
The main woman walks ahead, then suddenly turns around and walks backward while talking to the person filming.
She gets distracted by something behind the camera, turns forward quickly, and almost walks into her friend.
Everyone laughs naturally.
The camera keeps following them as the ocean becomes more visible, ending on an imperfect handheld view of the bright shoreline.

title: A Quiet Journey Through Hiroshima And Nagasaki
prompt: Create a 30 second photorealistic documentary style video in 1:1 aspect ratio, from a Japanese point of view, set in the early 1950s in Japan. The video should feel like authentic postwar Japanese documentary footage, as if filmed by a local reporter visiting Hiroshima and Nagasaki several years after the atomic bombings. Use black and white or slightly faded monochrome tones, soft contrast, visible film grain, light dust, minor scratches, subtle flicker, gentle handheld camera shake and realistic 1950s lens softness. No modern objects, no modern buildings, no text and no logos. The concept is a quiet spot review documentary. A Japanese male reporter in his late 30s walks through the preserved bombing areas, ruins, memorial remains and surrounding streets. He wears simple 1950s Japanese clothing, a dark jacket, plain trousers and worn leather shoes. His face should look serious, thoughtful and respectful. He speaks directly to camera in a calm documentary tone, as if showing the audience what remains of the bombing sites. The first part takes place in Hiroshima. Show broken walls, damaged foundations, memorial remains, open land, modest postwar reconstruction, bicycles, a few pedestrians and sparse trees. The reporter slowly walks through the site, looking around carefully. He gestures toward the remains and speaks quietly. Japanese dialogue “ここが広島の爆心地です。” “今も傷あとが残っています。” “静かですが、とても重い場所です。” The second part transitions naturally to Nagasaki. Show a different landscape with surviving ruins, damaged stone structures, memorial ground, hills in the distance and early postwar rebuilding. The reporter stands still for a moment, then continues walking and observing the surroundings. Japanese dialogue “こちらは長崎です。” “広島とはまた違う空気があります。” “ここに来ると、戦争の恐ろしさを強く感じます。” The final moments are reflective and emotional, not dramatic. The reporter faces the camera one last time while the background remains quiet and still. Japanese dialogue “この記憶を忘れてはいけません。” “二度と繰り返してはいけないと思います。” The camera style should feel like real 1950s Japanese documentary filmmaking. Slow pans, natural walking shots, simple compositions, respectful framing and realistic environmental detail. Focus on atmosphere, ruins, silence, human memory and postwar recovery. Keep the performance understated and natural. Audio should feel period accurate. Use outdoor ambience with light wind, distant footsteps, bicycle sounds, faint city movement and soft room tone like an old field recording. Add very subtle emotional documentary music underneath, using restrained strings, soft piano and minimal traditional Japanese tonal elements. Keep the music low so the reporter’s Japanese dialogue remains the main focus. Everything must feel historically grounded, realistic and respectful. No sensational action, no fantasy elements, no polished cinematic gloss and no exaggerated destruction. Preserve consistent character appearance, authentic 1950s Japan environment and believable documentary realism throughout.

承接机械狐回望。它转身跃进浅水区域，水下立刻依次升起六块布满青苔的圆形机械踏盘。摄影机从女主角身后沿连续弧线降低至水面高度，变为侧面平行跟拍。她位于画面左侧三分之一，前方留出踏盘和机械狐的移动空间。
机械狐踩过第一块踏盘，踏盘内部齿轮发出短促转动声；它跳向下一块后，上一块立刻缓慢沉回水中。女主角迅速理解规律，目光先锁定下一块踏盘，再移动身体。
她使用低高度、短距离跳跃：白色尖头鞋的前脚掌先落在踏盘干燥中心，膝盖弯曲吸收冲击，确认稳定后才蹬向下一块。每次踏盘受力，水面向外推出真实波纹，披纱末端扫过水面，留下逐渐扩大的湿痕。机械狐始终领先一块踏盘，不时回头确认她的位置。

摄影机沿栏杆继续向右滑行，绕过黄色机械支柱后贴近回廊侧壁。巨型设施因压力板被唤醒，上方卫星天线开始缓慢转向，沉睡多年的电机发出层层递进的低频轰鸣。

高跟鞋以短促前脚掌步伐落在木板中央，避免鞋跟卡入缝隙。一次机械支架突然向内折叠，她的鞋底轻微打滑，身体向左偏斜；她立刻抓住右侧护栏，以手臂拉力和腰腹力量把身体拉回路径。探险包撞击腰侧，湿润披纱在身后扬起，折叠线紧追脚跟。

女主角没有直接抢夺。她先放松肩膀，缓慢摘下探险包的搭扣，随后把戴着白色长手套的左手平稳伸向机械狐。机械狐注视她一瞬，主动低头，用前爪将金色机械种子推入她掌心。
种子接触手套的瞬间发出一次轻微机械心跳声。整座遗迹随之苏醒：头顶巨型卫星天线缓慢转向天空，黄色机械结构内部依次亮起温暖的琥珀色灯光，缠绕建筑的藤蔓轻微抖动，竹林深处传来连锁齿轮启动声。水池中的其他白色守护像同时转头望向她，但没有靠近。

**终态：**金色机械种子唯一地位于女主角左手掌心；机械狐坐在她右后方的石台上；整个竹林机械古寺正在逐层苏醒。
